messages.text: Nothing seems to happen.
You see no visible result.
Everything seems the same as before.

An iron door exists at the bottom of the pool of water.  Hardened tree gum forms a ring around the outside of the door.  Part of the tree gum has been torn.  The watertight seal is broken.  The bubbles are air escaping from below.
Wrenching on the iron ring, you thrust the door open.  Your gaze immediately falls on a lever as you gain entry.  Perhaps it's a device to operate a pump and drain unit.  Do you pull the lever?

A large drain opens in the floor of the pool and empties the water.  It will be an easy matter to leave this place now that you know what to do.  You hastily enter the tunnel below and push the lever back to its original position.

You slosh your way up the steep, sloping tunnel towards the surface.  The cold water steadily washes over your numbing feet.  Finally, you reach the door that leads to the false pool above.  You throw the lever to unseal it.  Ah!  Fresh air!

With anxious dread, you survey a gory scene.  Fully two dozen shadow elves lay bludgeoned to death near the entrance to the cave.  You inspect their wounds and determine that the murder weapons were a combination of axes and hammers.

The bodies have been stripped of any useful equipment.  A few loose strands of chain mail are scattered about.  The shadow elves' attackers felt the mithril in their armor and weapons was worth taking.
The attackers made a good effort to cover their tracks.  However, the Ranger in your party can make out their trail.  Do you wish to follow them and see where it leads you?

After several hours of fast tracking, the trail begins to fade.  The party you pursue ascended a solid rock plateau about 60 feet from the cavern floor.  Travel will be treacherous along the edge of this plateau.  Do you ascend?
Apparently, the retreating shadow elves did not have enough crew to man all the boats.  Some still remain.
The dead litter the ground like autumn leaves.  The bodies of approximately 150 shadow elf warriors sprawl across the battlefield.  Twelve of the dead were  slain by shadow elf weapons.
Were they slain by another tribe of elves or their very own troops? Failure in a given mission could notoriously result in death under shadow elf rule.
The great underdark river known as "Hell's Serpent".  Massive sailing ships thrust through the swirling waters.  Their mighty sails swell as jet streams of air blast through the underdark.
The ascent is tricky.  You must successfully perform an acrobatic act.  If you slip, 6 to 60 damage is taken during the fall.

An acrid smell assaults your nostrils.  Your gaze shifts along the edge of the plateau and eventually falls upon a large walled off cavern.  Drifting fumes provoke an image of fierce, radiant forges intermingled with the strong odor of dwarven mead.
Boisterous dwarven song breaks out from several different locations.  An immense, powerful dwarven clan has endeavored to make this section of the underdark their home.
Suddenly, from the darkness a deep voice calls out to you in common.  Klivrig: "You dar!  Stop where ye stand, or be squashed!"  Do you obey or attempt to hide in the nearby crags?

With crossbows raised, a large patrol of dwarven warriors closes in.  Their fingers poise for the kill.  They scrutinize you and attempt to determine your status as a threat.  Klivrig: "Hmmm.  Seems we got ourselves a bunch of sneak thieves."
The drake's body turns to stone.  Your weapon is trapped inside.  It transforms into petrified flesh.

The guardian's magical armor and weapon collapses.  Wispy tendrils slowly begin to seep from the armor's cracks.  A dark shadow rises and forms a macabre apparition.  With a vengeful shriek, it hurls and attacks.
An old ship is washed up on shore.  You board the ship to find several dead corpses rotting in the sun.  Most have had their throats cut.  One or two have been bound and beheaded on deck.
Stand fast
Try to flee
A pool of bubbling water stands amid a grassy field.  Several dead deer lie nearby, bloated by the scorching sun.  Strange that scavengers have not devoured the carcasses.

The leader pokes you several times with thick grubby fingers.  Klivrig: "Me thinks you be trying to sneak into me home.  What du ya tink about dat!  Ha!  You don't seem to be much worth our trouble.  Move along!"
With short legs and limited speed, the dwarven warriors are no match for your speed.  However, their familiarity with the terrain allows them to catch you easily.
The din of battle has captured the attention of another patrol.  They rush to aid their fellows in battle.
You manage to pull the lever on the other side of the iron bars.  The gate is quickly lowered.
A group of guards does not notice your approach.  It seems few visitors arrive unannounced.  You catch them by surprise as you approach.

Guard: "Hey!  Were did  you come from?  Stop right there."  Suddenly you are surrounded by several dozen dwarven warriors.  "Klivrig and his band must be sleeping out there.  How did you get past the pickets?"

"Never mind.  The fact is that your here and you don't seem to be much of a threat.  I assume you want to go inside.  Well in you go.  But mind you.  Don't make any trouble.  If you do, I will personally strip your hide from your bones."
"You got a filthy shadow elf with ya!  You murdering scum!"

As you attempt to catch your breath, you see a massive force of warriors forming a line some 50 meters to your north.  They are forming a solid wall of steel.  A number of clerics back them up from behind.  This does not look good.
You feel it best to retreat before an even larger group can form up and attack.  You beat a hasty retreat towards the west.
You manage to get to the small island in the middle of the lake.  An old dwarf is sitting outside the small hovel petting a small tarsk.  As you approach the tarsk leaps from his lap and runs away.

"Hulooooo!  You almost scared Samwise half to death.  Pay him no mind.  He is skittish in his old age.  Please join me."  The old dwarf shows absolutely no sign of fear or apprehension towards you.  He speaks to you as if you have been lifelong friends.

"Ooooooh!  I see you have shadow elves among you.  I should be careful not to get too close to the village.  They do so much hate them.  King Raggwine was slain in an elf attack near 400 years agone.  The new king, Newt Sniffelhoper has sworn revenge.
What is it you would like to do?

"If your inspectors, then I guess you have some kind of authorization to be here.  Let me see it if you please."  Do you attempt to talk your way out of the situation or do you refuse to show him anything.

"I think I have heard of this story before.  Do you know how it ends?  It ends up with me throwing you guys behind bars for a while until the captain can sort this out."  With that the man calls for the other guards to surround you.
You are hopelessly outnumbered.  Do you want to try and fight your way out of the room or do you let them take you into custody?
Alarm bells sound down the hall.  In the distance you hear shouts as men take up arms.  It's all you can do to escape the building without being seen.
Your description have been given to the town guard and every trooper is eager to avenge the death of their friends.
You have traveled the Realmz far and wide in search of adventure.  You must rest.   A nearby town may offer the comforts of home and the conveniences of city living.

Travel a few hours southward, and you will reach Winterhaven.  By all accounts, it is an incorruptible town.  A fair-minded city magistrate, a wise ruling council, and an honest merchant's guild have given Winterhaven a respectable reputation.
You look forward to a time of rest and relaxation.  Although small,  Winterhaven provides opportunities generally possessed by much larger cities.

A short distance to the east of Winterhaven lies Silver Peak, a large mountain range.  Within its confines is a metal  more precious than silver,  rarer than gold,  and capable of  countless uses.  Mithril - the famed metal.

Used by master craftsmen to create the finest arms and armor,  Mithril is known far and wide throughout the Realmz.  The rich caches of Mithril deep within this mountain have brought untold prosperity to  Winterhaven.

As you draw near the gates of Winterhaven your pace falters.  The strong,  sturdy gates are ajar.  Immense hinges bearing their great weight have been pried from the jam.  Guards in ordinary dress wander about the area.
A fit, young man asks you to state your business.  You inform him that you seek the comforts of a fine inn and wish to take up residence for a short while.

Guard: "You have come to the right place, my friends.  Not a better place to live for fifty leagues or more.  Times are a tad strange at present,  but I'm sure you will grow to love it here.  Most do."
You gaze about warily and inquire, "What do you mean,  times are strange?"  Thoughtfully scratching his tanned cheek,  the young guard searches for  a good explanation.
"For as long as I can recall, the dwarven clan Huchack has done all the mining for Mithril.  Now for the past several months, they have stopped bringing Mithril ingots to trade.

Times do get lean now and then, but they  always discover a new vein and Mithril starts to flow again.  However, it's been nearly seven months now, and we have not seen so much as a stone weight of raw ore.

It can't be lack of effort.  The clan Huchacks quartermasters have been buying every  pick, shovel, and necessary supply available.  Caravans even journeyed south to buy additional supplies from the Port Gillan miner's guild.

The town council and city magistrate have twice traveled to Silver Peak to speak with King Cormite - the leader of the Huchack clan.  He assured the council that it's just a matter of time before they find a new vein.
Rumors claim that the town council secretly cast a spell on Cormite to determine whether or not he spoke the truth.  It is widely believed  he was dishonest with the council during their meetings.

Such a spell can't reveal the truth behind the deceit.  The king refuses to give credence to our suspicions.  We have no thieves guild,  and the council cannot find anyone willing to steal into Silver Peak to discover the truth behind the missing Mithril.

The guard studies your group with a troubled,  yet hopeful stare.  "If it's adventure you seek,  talk with the council.  Every scrap of Mithril in town is in the process of being stolen.  Even the hinges on our front gates have disappeared."

"The blacksmith is forging a new set of iron hinges.  It will take time.  Till then, we must pull double shifts to guard the front gate.  I can't believe any danger would occur.  It's always been peaceful here."  The guard  looks about uncertainly.
As you ponder this information,  your eyes are drawn westward to a tall, ornate building.   Hmm...  the town council, perhaps?  You abruptly bid the guard good day and enter the city.

You enter a large room.  Rows of wooden bunks climb the walls.  A soldier on the way out collides with you.  Unperturbed,  you question why  the town guard is housed in such crowded, dismal quarters.  Guard: "Ah!  Now our gates hang open all the time.

The council hired extra guards.  No place to billet them in the regular barracks, so they stuffed us in here.  Not too many complaints, though.  I call 'em cozy quarters!"  With a leer of ghastly bad breath and a wicked jab to your side,  he exits.
A sturdy lock made from Mithril bolts the door shut.  You peer between two warped boards.   Beyond the door,  there appears to be several storage pits.  You're unable to determine what they contain.
The door slides open on well-oiled hinges.
The trap door in the floor opens easily.  However,  there is nothing in the storage bin below.

The room is filled with fresh supplies.  Flour bags,  pots of golden honey,  jugs of strong wine, strings of dried meat and bins of fruits and vegetables.  The fragrant intermingling of spices fill the air.   Your stomach growls audibly.
As you approach the foot locker at the end of the bed,  a hulky guard startles you.   "Don't  touch that!  The captain don't like people poking 'round his stuff.   What are you doing in here?"
Guard: "Thieves!  Stand alert, men!  We have thieves bold enough to steal right from under our noses!"

Guard: "Very well.  It's best if you excuse yourself from this area.  It's off limits without proper authorization.  If it's the captain your looking for, he's off to the east on a mission for the council."

You attempt to pump the man for more information on the captain.  Guard: "Captain Ramius is a brave man.  I believe he's been tasked with uncovering the mystery of the lack of Mithril coming from Silver Peak."

Don't tell anybody I said that.  It's not official, but I can read the runes on the wall.  Captain Ramius used to be an assassin for a mighty northern lord.  Ever since his wife Sara got him some proper churchin,  the man's become a model citizen."
The council convinced him to spy on the dwarves and discover the truth.  Now it's best that you go before the other men come snooping around.  I'm bucking for a promotion and don't want any trouble."

Guard: "And just who are you,  that you're so interested in the captain?  Listen to me!  He charged me with watching his stuff  till he gets back.  Until then, I'm in charge, and I don't want people poking around his stuff!"

The man mulls over your reaction.  Guard: "Hmmm.  Nobody but bloody bureaucratic inspectors would be so bold as to talk that way.  To be sure,  you are inspectors!  Captain Ramius is not here.  I imagine you'll

want to wait for him to get back before you go tearing into his foot locker.  If you look in there, mark in your report that I had nothing to do with it!"  The man sharply turns and walks away as if you smelled of rotten eggs.

The foot locker belonging to Captain Ramius sits unlocked on the ground.  Strange.  It  has no lock.  You scrutinize the outside carefully and lightly touch over the outer trappings.   No signs of a booby trap.   Do you want to look inside?

You wade through worn religious tomes and a mound of mundane toiletries.  A small brass key  has slithered its way to the bottom.  Due to a fear of inspection and a potential failure of meeting code,  you notice the guards pointedly avoid you.

When no one is looking,  you deftly open the locker.   You rifle your way through several tomes of a religious nature and a mound of mundane items.  In your haste, a small brass key almost escapes your attention.

At the bottom of the pit lies a small burlap sack.  Rats have chewed holes through it, and a foul odor does not encourage you.  With a stick,  you shred the sack apart.  Underneath the putrid body of an enormous rat lie several heavy Mithril ingots.

You find a small leather wrap wedged behind the statue and unfold the weighty packet.  Heavy hinges made of Mithril are revealed.  Aha!  The hinges to the main gate!  The thief stashed them here for safe keeping.
Your spine tingles in alarm as you enter a dirty room permeated by the smell of rotting flesh.  Evil rituals have been performed here.  Evil existing right under the council's very noses!
The foul stench is beyond compare.   A magical barrier must prevent the foul odor from leaving this room so that it can seep its way into the remains of the building.

Most of the webbed tomes on the shelves are common writings of the day.  However,  one dusted shelf  stands out from the rest.  You pull a few out.  Is that dried blood staining the covers?  The occupant of this dread cell seems to frequent this shelf.

You progress down the corridor.   Up ahead,  there is a hurried scuffling noise.  Before you can contemplate a reaction, a voice rings out.  "Hold, intruders!  Move no further or you shall surely die in your tracks!"
You frantically dash for cover back to the room.   A fireball blasts down the corridor.  Some of your party is unable to avoid a tender scorching before breaking for cover.

You must prepare to battle a damaging foe.   Surrounded by a shimmering translucent sphere,  a man in fine robes proceeds along the corridor.  He possesses a shell of anti-magic.  You do not bother to cast any spells.
"Thieves!  Why do you intrude into my most private chambers !"

"Fools.  Do you think that I am naive?  The only thing more distasteful than a liar and a thief is one who mistakes me for a simpleton."  He closes his eyes and claps his hands together.   Magic dances upon his lips.

The wizard mumbles a few words so ancient and powerful that even one of your experience has never heard the like.  A spray of golden sparkles flow from the wizard's fingers.  Small, hideous creatures spring from the floor around his feet.
Within moments, all manners of beasts grow to tremendous size.  They have one purpose to their existence - to obey the wizard's commands.  This does not bode well.

For a brief moment,  you feel dizzy.   Your mind is being scanned by the wizard!  He glowers with a captive glare,  "I do perceive that you stumbled upon this room without evil intent.  Your wills are very strong and I can't...
glean anything more from you directly.  Perhaps, you tell the truth in this matter.  I ask one simple question.  You shall answer directly or face dire consequences!  Do you intend me direct harm?"
Before you answer,  let it be known that I can detect deceitfulness and shall punish you with a painful death!"
You wish him no ill.
You desire to attack him.

You search his body and discover identification papers.  The man is Maxwell,  a member of the ruling council!   Charading as a goodly man he has managed to hide his   inner, evil intentions.  A small,  folded scrap of paper may shed some light.

"I may have some use for you.  My name is Maxwell.  My master is a powerful being.  The full extent and nature of his powers are unknown even to me.   At present, I am tasked to learn information on his behalf."
Maxwell's eyes bear down on you, "Perhaps, you could help me in this task.  I will overlook your intrusiveness in return for your aid in this matter."
Agree to aid him.
Decline his offer.
"Very good.  It's a simple task - one of  utmost importance to my master.   He has lost a powerful stone known as "The Geyser."

The stone was stolen.  My master would  sacrifice all for its return.  If you acquire any information leading to its whereabouts,  the reward would be profitable.  My master possesses great wealth and power.

I have but one possible clue.   My sources reveal unusual behavior on the part of some Dwarven clans.  These clans control the Mithril mines deep inside the eastern Silver Peak mountains.   My intuition believes that you should begin your search there.

"Begone!   Do not return unless you have information concerning the Geyser."  He throws out is his arms and towers over you.   A twisted, evil smirk with glowing eyes is the last thing you see.  Immediately, you are teleported away from his sanctuary.

"You show remarkable courage in the face of peril and are to be commended for your restraint.  Perhaps,  you are not  fools!"  You shift uncomfortably under his penetrating gaze.  "I am willing to look the other way and forgive...
your violation of my privacy.  If you aid me in my quest,  I will make it worth your while."
Nothing seems to happen.

Your mind is probed.   There are no words of communication.   However,  you have a deep sense of dread.  If you return without definite news of the Geyser, a swift, evil punishment will certainly befall you.  You shudder the sensation off.
Throw the lever?

You enter an overly ornate office and are immediately stopped by the desk clerk.  "The council is in session.  State your business,  if you please."  Do you make up a story in order to try and gain entrance to the council?

"Hmmm.  Very well.  But if I find you are not being truthful,  it will weigh against you if you need my assistance in the future.  Enter,  but be quiet until one of the guards brings you before the council."
"Halt!"  A large man in fine armor blocks your entrance to the council chamber.  He glances sharply at the clerk who slowly shakes his head.

"It's good that you kept your mouth shut out there.   I don't trust the clerk.   It's best that  we keep that one in the dark.   We do not want it to get out that  we're looking for people to go on a mission as dangerous and important as this."

I must admit  I didn't think we would get a group that looks so capable on such short notice.  Stand silent until I announce you to the council."  The guard approaches an official sitting at the head of the table.

He returns after a brief consultation.  Facing the council,  he proclaims, "I offer the council the first petitioners.  They have come in response to our silent decree."  With that he beckons you forward to stand before the council.

The council chamber is dominated by a long, dark table with tall, ornate chairs for the nine council members.  The head magistrate sits at the head of the table on a cushioned, ample throne of splendor.

One chair is empty.  The head magistrate notes your curious glance at the empty chair and interrupts your thoughts with a booming voice, "I am Braxis, head magistrate and leader of the great council of nine."

The council members nod in turn as Braxis introduces them.  "Stephens, Bolisven, Selbena, Gorimar, Chuldev, Brenvest, Victoria and Rodrigo.  The empty chair is Maxwell's.  Lately,  he's been frequently absent.  The head magistrate pauses and frowns.
Is it true you wish to enter into a contract on our behalf?  I must warn you.  The mission is potentially fraught with danger.   However,  if you  complete the task you will be well rewarded.
The very livelihood of our fair city is at stake, and we would pay much to insure the freedom and happiness of its citizens."  Intrigued,  you ask for more details before entering into a contract.
"I am afraid there is not much else I can reveal to you prior to your acceptance.  To be honest,  the nature of the contract requires you to search out vital information."  Do you accept?

"Very well.  We shall continue to look for someone to take this commission.  Do not tell anyone that we are looking for someone to carry out this mission.  Our silent decree shall reach only those capable of gathering information.
We must insure that new arrivals are skilled at detecting what is not easy to learn.  Good day, good people."  You are swiftly ushered out of the council chamber.
"Very good.  You seem a capable lot."  He nods approvingly.   "Draw closer to the table.  I will tell you all that I can.  Then you must depart in your search for information."
An extremely well-hidden passage to the north.  It is blind luck that you found it at all.  The precise craftsmanship must be the handiwork of dwarves.
Luckily,  you also have a dwarf in your group or you may never have located it.
You find a stash of wealth.  In addition, there are some items made of Mithril.  While sorting through the loot, you discover Mithril hinges designed for a heavy gate.
Some abominable creature has been slain and left for dead.  The skeleton is like no creature you have ever seen, alive or dead.  The eye sockets in the skull are huge.
It must have been an underground dweller.  Creatures with eyes this big must have lived very deep.   You ponder how it could have reached the land's surface.   Do you pick through the remains?
You peel back the rotting flesh hoping to find something of interest.  A small glint of gold catches your eye.  There is a torn, small fold of leather in the robe.   A secret pocket!
The leather has rotted to the point of revealing the once hidden artifact.  It's also home to a disgusting mass of carrion grubs.
Who will be so brave?
You quickly scrape the vermin away before they can penetrate too deep.  However, they manage to nearly paralyze you.
Try and talk.
Refuse strongly!
Fight.
Run away.

You search the dresser and find expensive cloth embroidered with the name "Sir Maxwell".   Such fine stitchery would indicate that the council member Maxwell had once been a high knight of a royal court.

You discover a false panel in the bottom drawer and pull out a leather bound diary.  Most of it is written in the large hand of a small child and fails to catch your interest.  However, the last few pages are obviously written by an adult.  It reads...
A sign posted on the wall warns that only authorized council members may enter this area.  You are NOT to enter this room.

You have locked yourself in.  Guards rapidly arrive to see what has triggered the alarm.  "This area is clearly off limits!  You better have a good explanation for being in there!"  Quickly, the bars are released.

"You're the people commissioned to carry out the council's secret mission.  I probably shouldn't do this, but I'm going to release you.  Be more careful in the future.  I don't know the details of your mission, but I am aware that it's most important."
You are immediately released, and the guards disperse.  You are surprised and relieved.  Apparently, having a personal relationship with the council has its bonus privileges.

You're in direct violation of council orders which clearly state that this room is to be clear of civilians at all times.  Now you could end up in the stockade.  Guards cart you off to a holding cell to wait  judgment.
The guards lock you in the cell and leave.  You decide that it's best to wait patiently until you can explain your mistake.

A man dressed in a majestically rich robe comes to visit you.  He is accompanied by one lone guard.  "Dear people,  it would seem you are in need of assistance.  We could use people of your obvious talent.  We are willing to free you in exchange...
for a minor service.  Under the circumstances,  I would urge you to accept my offer."

A tray of unguarded vials lays in open sight.  Someone feels that a mere warning sign is enough to keep out intruders.  Either they're very trusting around here or extremely negligent.  Do you pilfer the vials?

He releases you and presents you to the town clerk.  With suspicion, he informs the clerk that you are here to see the council. The displeased clerk frowns.  He briskly motions you into the council chamber and instructs you to keep your mouth shut.
The council wishes you speed and good fortune on your quest for knowledge.  You are urged to continue your journey.   With a signal wave, guards wisk you out the door.
Using the small brass key you obtained from Captain Ramius's foot locker,  you open the gate and step inside.
There is a small keyhole in the wall.  Nothing you have fits the lock.   Your numerous efforts to pick the lock or use magic to bypass the gate prove fruitless.

You are about to step into the pit and investigate further when a noisy clamor projects from the hole.  You hastily back away.  An immense, armored body thunders out of the pit.  With drawn sword, he demands, "Who are you?  How did you get in here?"

An engraved emblem displayed on his chest plate establishes that he's the captain of the guard.  You tell Captain Ramius that you have been commissioned by the council to uncover the secret behind the lack of Mithril.  Ramius: "Your grasp of the situation

and the fact that the council has been looking for someone to undertake this secret mission is proof enough you speak the truth.  However, it doesn't explain how you obtained a copy of the gate key.  There are only two copies and one is locked away.
How did you procure the other key?  It was safely stowed in my foot locker under a Mithril lock!"  You reveal that his chest was missing its lock.  Thus,  you obtained the key with little effort.

Ramius: "Blast it!  Thieving rogues!  They're stealing every scrap of Mithril available.  I'd like to march to Silver Peak and force them to return what's rightfully mine.  That cost me 50 gold talons!"  Noticing your puzzled expression,  he explains.

Ramius: "I have determined that all the Mithril disappearing from town has been stolen by the dwarves from Silver Peak.  So many of them travel about town now on the pretense of purchasing supplies,  no one has discovered their true intentions.

The livelihood of our fair city is so heavily dependent on them that no one dares to question them or stand in their way.  For some covert purpose they're collecting every scrap of Mithril in existence.  I was unable to gain access to their warren,

but there were indications that they are stockpiling all the Mithril in a central storehouse deep within the mountain.  Obviously, we have both been commissioned by the council to uncover the truth.   Why not work together to insure our success?"

I have to pick up more supplies and take the time to inhale a decent meal.  Then we can head out.  Everyone is counting on us to ascertain why the Dwarves are suddenly ruled by such greedy desire.  Fate is in the balance."

You accompany Ramius back to his barracks. He rudely kicks his unlocked footlocker as if willful desire will make the lock magically reappear.  He remarks with disgust, "If there's one thing that's worthless,  it's an unlocked footlocker."

Once, somebody stole my jelly donut when I  accidentally left it unlocked!"  You proceed to a tavern and relish a hearty, heavy meal.  Afterwards,  Ramius purchases supplies until his sack bursts with gear.  You return to the pit where you met earlier.
Ramius: "I'm all set.  This tunnel exits just east of town.  I hired a few hungry gnath to dig it.  Dug the entire course in only three days.  Those boys really work up a sweat."

My returns and departures must remain  secret.  I'd like to prevent the dwarves from discovering we are spying on their activities.  By the way,  I'd appreciate the return of my key."  You apologetically reproduce the key and set off for Silver Peak.

The pit exits into a small clearing east of town.  Farther east is the distant Silver Peak.  The captain whips open his sack and withdraws a small whistle.  "This whistle possesses magical properties.  It was a gift from Rodrigo of the city council."
If dire trouble arises, a single blow will teleport us back to a spot just north of  the town.  Unfortunately,  the magic will only work once.  Keep it.  I trust you will use it wisely."

"I might be weak-minded after a long day's trek and blow it just to save my poor blistered feet additional suffering."  Although you doubt this explanation for the gift,  you are touched by his generosity and express heartfelt  thanks.

You gently blow the crystal whistle.  It appears as if nothing happened.  However, you are no longer where you were before.  An unimaginably smooth teleport.  No dizziness.   No nausea.   Rodrigo must be highly skilled.

You travel further east traversing the land as it begins its ascent up Silver Peak.  Eventually,  the ground becomes cooler and  covered in the permanent snow of higher elevations.  A cold stiff wind blows continually chilling you to the bones.
Ramius gasps into the wind, "We're almost there.  Just a little farther.  We need to travel a bit more east.  The range is dead ahead.  We can enter the dwarven warrens at the southern point."

"It would be best to reach our destination and make camp before nightfall.  These mountains are full of snow beasts.  Recently,  they have become unusually bold and aggressive.  They used to retreat at the mere sight of a man.

I believe we're safe for now.  They're normally active at night."  A loud bellow startles you from behind.   You whip around to see muscular snow beasts emerge from the powdery,  blowing snow.  Caught off guard,  Ramius splutters,  "What!  How's this?"

Though wounded, it appears that Ramius will  be alright.  "The council was lucky to engage you for this mission.  A more stalwart bunch I have never seen.  If only I had a dozen more like you, I would storm the warrens and solve this problem by force."

As it stands now, we should strive to keep as low a profile as possible.  Quick!  We must cover the bodies and trails of blood.  Move!  Tarry here too long and we'll attract the attention of a dwarven patrol."
Far off  in the distance,  a group of tremendous beasts have gathered.  They appear to be 30 hands high or more.   Do you wish to attack them?

Some frozen corpses.  Their blood stains the snow.   They are dressed in the manner of peasants, but your suspicion is aroused.   The garments are unusually clean.  No patches.  No signs of wear and tear.  The footgear looks new and hardy.

Ramius:  "It appears that Winterhaven is not the only one interested in discovering the truth.  This crew had bad luck.  It's strange that the dwarves just abandoned these corpses so near the warren's entrance.

Your attempt has failed.
Your in!

Empty.  You take a step and slide to the floor on an old scrap of paper.  Annoyed, you snatch at the cause of your downfall.  The paper is actually a map that reveals how to trigger a magic portal.  This portal allows one to escape from the dungeon.
A locked door.   However, this one has been recently reinforced.  It will not be easy to break.
Bloody footprints begin at the entrance to this room.  The footprints disappear into a pool of sickly fluid at the room's north end.

A few cleaning supplies - soap and scrub brushes.  Why would undead creatures be concerned with washing their hands before eating?  It doesn't make any sense.

A crowd of rowdy, undead knights indulge at the table.  The plates of food have long since decayed into ashes, yet they guzzle it down like a sumptuous Christmas feast of spiced who-onions and roast who-beast.
A few of the skeletal figures mill about near the room's entrance.  When you burst in,  they howl and close in to attack.  Their screams of outraged epithets haunt your ears.

Upon the deaths of their comrades,  the remaining knights tear themselves away from their phantom meal and attack with zeal.  One knight alone refuses to participate.  He watches the battle as if it were a play put on for his own personal amusement.

The lone knight  floats over to you.   He makes no move to attack.  Weary from battle, you are loathe to instigate another.  There is something unusual about this particular knight.  You gaze into the closed helm and are shocked to see flesh on bones.

The knight suddenly flips his visor up to reveal the flesh and bones beneath the armor.  Volmax: "Ah!  Shall I curse you or thank you?  Those men...   Yes, they were men once, pledged to defend me in days long past.

They fell on the field of battle due to my poor judgement.  I was a coward.  I watched them die and never once ventured from the safety of my post.  They cursed me with their dying breaths.  All were slaughtered while attempting to defend my castle.

Ever since, I have been cursed to relive that fateful battle time and time again.  Morbius freed me from this curse.  He once again bent their undead souls to defend me.   I did not know how dear the cost would be to release me from my private hell.

He said that I would never again have to witness my men being slaughtered if I but pledged myself to aid him in his cause.  I gladly did so.  Alas!  Since then I have been cursed to live a life of solitude among my own men!

They go about eating and drinking food and wine only they can see and taste.  I am forced to watch them revel and tell stories of glories past.  Through all of this, they do not speak to me or even look in my direction.
Now they are destroyed.  My curse is lifted, and I can once again seek peace and prosperity.  Help me escape this foul prison! I am held here by a twist of fate.

Only my men knew the secret magic word.  Once uttered,  the ward guarding the door would be destroyed.  Yet, they never spoke to me.  Now they're truly dead, and I will never know.  Under the circumstances, I wonder if I should view you as friend or foe.
Destroy this accursed ward,  so that I may leave this hateful place.  Can you help me?
"Foes!  You've made your choice!  I cannot bear this endless torment!  Doomed to a life such as this!  You will die at my hand!"
"I and my men thank you.  May they now rest in peace."
The glyph begins to glow slightly.  There is a bright flash.  Arcs of energy bolt from the glyph's center and strike everyone in the room.
The glyph begins to glow slightly.   Soft, mystical music pleasantly hums an intricate rhythm.   You feel peaceful and warm from the glow.

Taking Volmax by the hand, you lead him past the glyph.  Volmax breaks out in scornful laughter.  "I'm free!  Free!   Mortals!  You're easy targets.  It's true,  I'm Morbius's prisoner,  but the circumstances are not what you think.

I am one of few that can match him in power and ability.  Those undead knights were not my former men.   They were here to prevent me from escaping.  Now that the glyph is destroyed my magical powers have been restored.
Mortal fools!  Morbius shall suffer dearly  for his crimes and so shall you!

Volmax: "Fools!   What you have done?  Morbius is extremely close,  hence I am unable to regenerate.  The horror!  The horror!"  Volmax shrieks in agony.  His litch body writhes wildly about.  It fails to form completely and vanishes.
Ramius: "His destruction is due to the fact that he could not regenerate while being in such close proximity to another litch.  This knowledge may be useful if we encounter Morbius."

Captain Ramius studies the broach found on Volmax. "This is like no broach I've ever seen.  Microsopic writing covers the entire piece.  I'm unfamiliar with these symbols.  We would need a microscope and a decoder.  I'm afraid I can tell you nothing."

You discover 13 stone coffins.   You have already encountered numerous undead and evil beasts while wandering through this dreadful fortress.  You fervently hope that any potential inhabitants are incapacitated.  Meanwhile,  it's best to avoid contact.
However,  the biggest rewards often go to the ones who are willing to take the biggest risks.  Do you pry open a coffin lid and check out the contents?

You start to pry open the lid on one of the coffins.  Immediately,  the lids on all the other coffins open an equal amount.  You quickly slide the lid back in place.  The others slide back in place as well.
This will be an all or nothing situation.  Do you still want to risk it?
Again you shift the lid off of one coffin.  They all move.  You topple the lid onto the floor and look down inside.  Small piles of dust are all that remains of this once living creature.

Dissatisfied with your findings,  you search every inch of the area.  Several torches have been placed in prominent, high positions near the coffins.  On impulse,  you remove a torch from its ornate holder and toss it inside the coffin.
Suddenly, the lid lifts from the floor and floats back into place over the coffin.  It slowly comes to rest and seals the torch inside.  Do you wish to repeat this on all the torches?
One by one you repeat the process until all the coffins are once again closed and the torches are inside.  However, when complete you notice nothing else out of the ordinary.

You stand before the most ornate coffin you have ever seen in your lives.  It's carved from a solid crystal of amethyst and intricately carved.  There does not seem to be any visible seem from where the lid meets the bottom.

As you caress the smooth surface searching for a way in you hear shuffling from behind you.  Around the corner to the south you see a band of creatures stumbling your way.  Exactly 13 in number it is easy to figure out where they came from.

These creatures are simply huge and very slow moving.  Giant zombies is the only way to describe them.  Though they are slow they have managed to surround your avenue of escape and you are forced to confront them.
You have destroyed one of the unique crypt things.  As it crumbles into pieces a blast of energy emanates from it and recharges all those that remain.
Bashing away at the large steel gargoyle you literally smash it into pieces.  Before your very eyes the pieces reform into smaller yet perfectly formed steel gargoyles.
Bashing away at the medium steel gargoyle you literally smash it into pieces.  Before you very eyes the pieces reform into smaller yet perfectly formed steel gargoyles.
An extremely large iron statue of a gargoyle.  The craftsmanship is amazing as it looks as if it could almost come alive.

The statue along the west wall shifts to stare at you.  The steel gargoyle is moving!  It slowly stretches its wings and legs as if waking from a long winters nap.  An erie red glow comes from its eyes.  It lumbers forward to do battle.
As you are resting from that awesome battle suddenly you hear a small musical riff come from within the coffin.  You hear a strange sound coming from the west wall.
As formidable as this steel gargoyle is you are sure that a single foe, no matter how fierce should be of little challenge after the mighty battle you just won over the Crypt Things.
Your earlier assessment of a single creature being easy pickings was obviously wrong.  A dozen of those creatures could spawn an army large enough to overrun a fair sized city!
This crate contains some food stuffs you can use.
The footlocker is locked but easily broken into.  Inside you find some useful items.
You see a short hallway that looks to be used quite often as you see no dust on the floor.  This appears to be a safe place to rest.
One of the stones in the side of the wall catches your eye.  You quickly pull the stone from the wall and find a small button behind it.  Do you want to push it?
You hear a small click and a spring slide into place somewhere south of you.
A pit trap!  All characters not able to Save Vs. Dexterity at a -5 penalty stumble and fall in.
Drat!  Poison spikes!  Those that fell in must Save vs. Poison or be poisoned.  The only good news is that the pit was not deep and those that fell in can easily climb out.
The mirror looks to be of a magical nature.  You are aware that magical mirrors are often used to teleport to a different location.  You want to walk into the mirror to see where it takes you?

Huge piles of dung have been deposited in the corner by the Suckyolotol.  All manners of bones and debris can be seen jutting from the dung heap.  Arms and legs of being unknown jut from the disgusting mass.
As you slip and slide towards the corner you feel your very body being assaulted by parasites of every kind.  Save vs. Vitality as -3 or become diseased.
Those failing to Save vs. Vitality contract a disease.
Suckyolotol are capable of digesting almost anything, to include most objects made from the hardest of steel.  Magical items however can resist the digestive juices of even the most robust gut.
As you open the door to continue your search of the area you stumble upon a barracks full of guards.
More troops from further back in the room have moved forward.  They are a bit more disciplined because of the presence of a few high level magi.

As the dead pile up at your feet you see a figure even larger than the ogres.  A large ice giant is herding ogres in  your direction from the very back of the room.  You see it quaffing a large number of magical potions as it prepares to do battle.
A number of books of little interest and a few vials populate this large bookcase.
You gaze past the carnage to a spot in the back of the room.  All of the bunks seem of the size for ogres save the one towards the back which must have belonged to the ice giant.
Mostly personal items sized for a giant and of little use to you.  Save a few magical potions.

A man in fine red robes in on his knees with a dagger in hand trying to scrape a piece of something sticky off of the floor.  As you approach he hears you coming and mutters to himself.  Oleo: "Oh Dear!"

Oleo: "Sorry I did not hear you come in.  I was trying to clean up a bit around here."  He quickly trots past you and moves behind his desk while hiking his robes up over his feet to keep them from dragging on the floor.

He is moving so quickly it nearly makes you dizzy just watching him.  A pair of thick monocles cover his eyes.  They appear to aid him in his site only somewhat.  He squints at some parchment on his desk.

Oleo: "Lets see... Now I don't see anything about new arrivals here in my ledger.  Perhaps I was not informed.  Do you have your papers with you?  No... I don't suppose you would.  Hmmm. Well... Hmmm.  I say, I am at my wits end here.

The best I can do is offer to put you up on the barracks next door for now until I receive word on what it is I am supposed to assign you to.  By the looks of you I see that you are not to be used as simple guards.

Oh!  I may.... yes.. yes..  Ah!  Here it is."  Oleo picks up a rather large piece of parchment sealed with a wax emblem of a human skull.  He quickly uses his dagger to break the seal and reads aloud.

Oleo: "Well, it seems I am to send you on a mission to find something by the name of "The Geyser".  You inform him that you were under the impression that Morbius was already in possession of the artifact.  Oleo: "Oh heavens no!
If that was the case I would imagine he would not have sent for the Acid Claw Brigade to help track it down."  Suddenly he begins to speak a bit more quietly, almost as if to himself.

Oleo: "If indeed you are from the Acid Claw Brigade you should have been aware of that fact.   Oh no!"  He quickly grasps inside his robe and snatches a small sack of stones.  He does not hesitate a bit as he tosses them at your feet.
The stones quickly summon aid as Oleo attempts to retreat out the door.  Do you try and stop Oleo?

You quickly block his path.  Oleo: "Please, let me pass.  My pets will not discriminate.  They will be as happy to have my blood on their claws as yours.  TOO LATE!"  He cowers beneath his desk as you are beset by demons!
As you slay the Xonokite you gaze on in horror as it turns to stone trapping  your weapon inside.

As you retrieve your weapons from the stone bodies of the slain Xonokite.  You quickly turn your attention to Oleo who is still cowering under his desk.  He seems amazed that he has survived the ordeal.

Oleo: "You are indeed strong to have survived an attack by so many Xonokite.  I thought for sure my rash act had cost us all our lives.  I see now that I may have misjudged you.  You appear to be no friend of Morbius and thus we should work together.

I have not long been in the employ of Morbius but I wish I had never heard of him.  I was tempted into his employ with the offer of some arcane knowledge.  For one such as myself the chance to learn the arts of everlasting youth were difficult to resist.
I should have known that Morbius was just holding out a carrot.  If you are here to destroy Morbius as I think you are then perhaps I can aid you after all.
Oleo bolts out the door and slams it in your face.  Before you can even consider going after him you are set upon by huge demons.
Though I am no match for the likes of Morbius perhaps together we could defeat him.  Shall I join you in your quest?
Let Oleo Join You
Refuse his company
Oleo: "Very well.  Here, take this as it will help you in your quest.  He quickly hands you one of his monocles.  As you examine the wonderful craftsmanship you look up to find Oleo gone.
Oleo gathers a few possessions from his desk and joins your band.  Oleo: "How I have longed for this day.  I will see Morbius perish by my own hand or die in the trying!"

Moisture covers the floors.  In some places it is ankle deep.  Your hear the sound of slaves working near a large pool of water to the south.  A huge gang of chained trolls are digging holes in the stone floor.
It appears that there was some sort of underground spring that has begun to well up from the floor and slaves are trying to contain the water flow by digging pits.

A huge troll of a different type is whipping the worker trolls to make them work harder.  A pair of the workers stop for a moment to catch their breath and one spots you.  To your surprise he does not raise an alarm.

As the two trolls whisper in quiet tones the overlord sees them slacking and begins to whip them.  As the overlord is beating one poor wretch he spots you as well.  He commands the slaves to attack you.
With the overlord slain the workers stop their attack.  Though they are trolls and tend to be extremely evil at best, they realize that you are no friends of the overlord.

One troll steps forward.  Even as a large wound on his forearm seems to regenerate before your very eyes he speaks.  Noolum: "We want to be free.  We do not want to hurt tiny people.  We want to go home.  We have been force to work here long time.

Free us and we will help you if we can."  The workers are chained in pairs to the floor with a large iron pin.  They can wander about the area but can't flee unless released.  Do you trust Noolum and free the trolls or do you press home the attack?
Free The Trolls
Attack The Trolls
Balling up their mighty fists the trolls near you defend themselves as best they can.
Not wanting to be slaughtered like their brethren the rest of the slaves attack you.
Guarding this doorway is a powerful force of Death Stalkers.  The mounds of rotting flesh reeks of death and decay.
The din of battle has attracted a roving band of guards!
Noolum and his band of trolls you set free come to your aid to help you defeat the guards!
A few of Noolum's fellow trolls show up and lend aid.
The foul dank smell of death is upon you.  Your teeth chatter as you steel yourself against the unnatural cold of this room.  Such a place can be the resting place of only one as evil as Morbius.
With Morbius more akin to death incarnate than anything else you have ever encountered you should prepare yourself before getting any closer.
This chest contains wealth.
You stand before a large glyph on the floor to this room.  You see many chests stacked about the room.
A booming laughter echoes in the small chamber.  It comes from everywhere and nowhere all at once.
An image of Morbius appears before you.  Morbius: "We meet yet again.  I must admit I find your tireless pursuit of me a bit irksome.  However, every wolf has flees.  Tis easy enough to scratch!"
In a flash Morbius pulls one of his old tricks.  He conjures duplicates of himself.  Only one of which you know to be real.  But which one?

You pull out the stick pin you collected from the corpse of Volmax and hold it before you.  Morbius shrieks in terror!  Morbius: "Fools!  Do not bring that dark relic near me."  You quickly thrust it into his chest where it begins to pulsate.
The dark essence of Volmax within the relic pulses into Morbius.  Having broken the concentration of Morbius he fails to maintain his spell of duplication.
As the relic holding the essence of Volmax is embedded in his chest it feeds on his magical powers leaving him weak and unable to cast spells.
He runs around like a caged animal searching his robes for a small figurine.  He pulls it out and tosses it at your feet where it shatters into a dozen pieces.

You have slain Morbius.  With his material form destroyed, the Stick Pin that contains the essence of Volmax has kept him from reforming.  His essence joins that of Volmax trapped inside the Stick Pin.  There the two will wage a battle eternal.

Their trapped energies will remain imprisoned in the Stick Pin and their power will aid any who wears the pin until it is destroyed.  If used for good, the Stick Pin will serve as proof that sometimes it's possible for "Two Wrongs To Make A Right."
With the essence of Morbius and Volmax under your control you contemplate the true location of "The Geyser".
You have destroyed only an image of Morbius.  Morbius quickly projects another image to take its place.
You have destroyed the physical form of Morbius.  However, there is nothing to prevent him from reforming a new material form right before your eyes!
Morbius attempts to use his magic to escape.  He teleports only a short distance before his magic fails.

Inside the casket you find the original body of Morbius.  The curse of being a litch has been broken and the remains are now truly lifeless.   You search the inanimate corpse of Morbius and turn up a puzzling scroll along with a great sum of wealth.

One would not expect a litch to be interested in wealth.  The reason for the stores of treasure are clear after you read the scroll.  His vile and evil presence will not be missed.  The corruption, pain and death he has wrought has come to an end.
Every party member gains a level!
By the gods!  The floor seems to come alive and tries to eat you!

You see a large number of skeletons heaped about the floor.  Most are still wearing what armor or clothing they had on them at the time of death.  It was as if they were swallowed whole then spit out again after they were digested.
This corpse has a few magical items that survived the gut of those that made a meal of this poor soul.
Several large portions of the walls have caved in.  The water has eaten away at the mortar and caused the large stones to collapse into heaps.

Even as you examine the area you see a large section of wall collapse.  It would seem this fortress is falling prey to natural forces.  Unfortunately the section that just collapsed blocks the way you came in.
You cleave this whelp in two only to have two similar whelps attack.
You manage to push aside the earth that is blocking your way and reveal another room on the other side of the north wall.
You stand in a soggy mess as the walls crumble around you.  What is it you would like to do?
You manage to break some earth loose but there is just too much in the way.  Digging by hand would take forever.
You hear the something slithering behind you.  Out from the pool of water crawl some hideous... things!
May the makers have mercy on your soul!  A large number of things are crawling out of the pool of water and coming in your direction.  A few of them are huge in size and appear to be quite hungry.
You enter a large hall with no apparent way in or out.  Your special handiwork allowed you to get in but you do not see any natural means of entry or exit.
The northern section of the wall in this large room has seen major collapse damage.  If you are going to dig your way out perhaps the north wall may be your best bet.
You find a trap door that leads outside the castle walls.  As you gaze back towards the fortress you see it slowly begin to sink into the soggy ground.
However, there must be some way in or out as this large room is not altogether empty.  A large group of Acid Claw Warriors appear to be waiting around.
Their commander near the back sizes you up.  Your mode of entry makes it clear that you don't belong here but he does not know what to make of you.

Suddenly his eyes begin to squint as he takes note of your blood soaked clothing and the large amount of wealth you are carrying.  Gail Wyrmrider: "Well boys, looks as if we have some thieves trying to make off with our pay.
A thousand golden zarks to each man who cuts one of these skunks down!"

It is your best guess that Morbius was to meet with this group and take possession of "The Geyser".  Morbius may be able to come and go in a flash of magic, but these men surely could not.  Just how they arrived here is a mystery.
It would seem that without Noolum and the other Troll slaves the fortress was doomed to be sucked below the mire.  A fitting burial for Morbius to be sure.
In any case, "The Geyser" is now in your possession and perhaps with its power Weston will be able to construct his Mithril Vault after all.
You enter the council chambers to report your progress.  Ramius informs them of your adventures.  He fills them in on the plight of Weston, King Cormite and of your recovery of "The Geyser"

Many of the members are shocked to learn of the details of your journey.  Braxis: "I am simply amazed that you lived to tell the tale.  If indeed what you say is true, and I have no reason to doubt your word then we may yet be in danger.

Whoever, or whatever is the rightful owner of "The Geyser" will not doubt be wanting it back.  Those that master such relics as this must have a way of tracking them.  Be that the case then I can only assume that we can expect visitors.

Visitors of the most unwelcome sort."  Braxis turns to his fellow council members.  Braxis: "We must prepare!  I am a believer in preparing for the worst.  Assemble the command staff of the town militia.  We must make ready for battle.

You my friends must see to it that this hornets nest we have stirred up does not go for naught.  I bid you to take this relic and rush with great haste to the chambers of King Cormite.  This Mithril Vault must be completed.
Though it may mean the lack of Mithril in our fair city for some time yet to come I see no other choice.  We shall make preparations here to defend ourselves should the need arise.

I suggest you make great haste to return the relic to King Cormite and this Weston fellow.  The construction of the Mithril Vault may very well be the key to our long term survival."  With that Braxis turns to his fellow members to discuss preparations.

Ramius: "My duty is here my friends.  We have traveled far together and I count you among my most trusted of friends.  Few can face death and spit in its eye as you have.  I feel we shall fight side by side again some day.  Farewell"
You enter the chambers of King Cormite.  You are quickly ushered before the king to make your report.

The king is shocked to learn of the details of your journey.  Cormite: "I am simply amazed that you lived to tell the tale.  If indeed what you say is true, and I have no reason to doubt your word then we may yet be in danger.

Visitors of the most unwelcome sort."  Cormite turns to an aid.  Cormite: "Summon Weston to my chambers at once.  We have must work to do and precious little time to do it.  With the aid of this relic I believe we can yet construct vault in time.
However, we have to make sure we keep it.  If we are attacked by those that would seek its return we must rebuff them at all costs."
The king is about to make another statement when you suddenly hear warning horns.  A young dwarf rushes into the kings chambers without stopping to be introduced.

A mixture of excitement, fear and panic are awash upon the young dwarfs face.  Henril: "My king!  We are under attack by... by the gods know what."  Cormite: "Hold son!  Remain calm... Where is this attack and by how strong a force?"

Henril: "They are assaulting the warren entrance even now.  I am not sure as to the size of the attacking force but from what I saw it was massive in size.  A mix of beasts such as the likes as I have never seen nor heard tell of.

Huge armored beasts, as well as walking insect men that move with the speed of devils.  I even saw beasts that suck the brains from those they can grab.  I fear we must rally to the fight or our brothers at the entrance will soon be overrun!"

Cormite: "This be it then.  Muster every dwarf.  Pull the workers from the mines.  Tell them to keep their picks and shovels as we have no time to arm them properly." Cormite leaps off his throne and dashes out the door with you in tow.
Wounded but not dead King Cormite begins to slowly stand.  He kisses his sword and thanks it for its regenerative powers.  Once again it has saved his life.
King Cormite: "I can't believe that this small band was intended to defeat us.  Me be thinking it was a trick."

Suddenly a wounded dwarf staggers towards the king.  It's Henril!  Henril: "Me king!  Was an ambush.  No sooner did you leave your chambers than more of these foul vermin boiled up from below the floor.

The chamber guards fought as best they could but they were slaughtered.  It was all I could do to escape to warn you.   It's gone.  The relic you had us secure in your chambers was taken by the creatures."
Gritting his teeth in rage the king shouts at the top of his lungs!  King Cormite: "Damn be my hide!" and rushes off to his chambers to see for himself.

The king is furious for having been so foolish as to leave the relic so poorly guarded.  King Cormite: "We have no choice but to pursue these beasts and retake the relic.  I shall take personal command of this expedition.
We will recapture this relic or I will die trying!  Selecting six of his best warriors you journey into the tunnel in pursuit of the relic.
You see a group of hostile alien creatures stalking about.  Do you wish to engage them in combat?

You approach a pair of large buildings.  You stare in amazement as they seem to be constructed out of metal!  In all your days you have never seen such a thing.  Suddenly you hear a whirring sound from behind you.

You quickly spin around and draw steel but are simply too stunned by what you see to react.  You gaze upon a huge humanoid form.  It is constructed of metal and carries a weapon of a type you have never seen before.
You think back to the strange description of the beam weapons described by Gail Wyrmrider in his report to Morbius.  As you stand stunned it speaks to you in a strange but understandable voice.

Galactic Centurion (GC): "You there!  This is a restricted area.  What is your reason for being here?"  If this metal man was allied with those that have taken "The Geyser" you are convinced that it would have attacked without asking questions.

You press your luck and answer by telling it the truth.  After a short period it speaks.   (GC): "This Geyser you seek.  It is also what we seek.  We refer to it as a Gridstone.  It is a device that can generate huge amounts of power.

Those structures below are the last remaining outpost of those known as the Golians.  They are a vile and hated race throughout the galaxy."  You interrupt to ask what a galaxy is?   (GC): "I do not want to burden you with such things.

I will say just this.  These Golians should not be here on your world and I am part of a force known as the Galactic Centurions.  We are to retrieve the Gridstone and to exterminate the Golians for their crimes.

You may want to stand back as we are about to assault the fortress below.  For many cycles we have been in pursuit of the Gridstone.  We were fortunate that an accident caused their craft to crash on this world.

In the Golians attempts to escape they entered the forbidden sector.  Your world lies within this forbidden sector."  Cormite: "Why is our world forbidden?"  (GC): "It is not just your world but many such worlds in this area of the galaxy.

Your world has a core made from a substance that radiates a force you call magic.  We are from a world without such a substance and have developed along a different path than your world.  As you may guess, our two worlds are like oil and water.

Though your worlds do not possess it, we have the ability to travel between worlds much as you would ride a cart to the next town.  As such it is forbidden for those from our worlds to enter the forbidden sector.
The Golians violated that rule and have been sentenced to extermination.  We are here for just that reason.  Even now our assault force approaches to put an end to this chase once and for all."

A blazing flash of light and an explosion marks the end of the metal man who stood before you.  It erupts into a ball of flame before your eyes.  You spin to see a large group of creatures headed your way from the metal fortress.

Even as you dive for cover into the rocks nearby you hear another force coming from the north.  It must be the Galactic Centurions coming to assault this fortress.  It would seem you are stuck in the middle.

One of the GC comes to you to thank you in your aid in their battle.  (GC): "I wish to thank you for your aid in our fight.  At first we thought it was you that destroyed our scout.  We quickly realized that it was the Golians.
They must have spotted him while he was talking with you.  I listened in on your conversation." Suddenly you hear a commotion coming from the metal fortress.

The gates on the iron fortress open and a huge force comes out.  (GC): "My god!  We had no idea that they had begun to create a robotic force!  We need to retreat until we can bring our heavy weapon to the front.  Too late!"

The robotic force from the fortress quickly attacks you and your GC allies.  The first robotic forces to arrive are the smaller craft that literally fly through the air.  The area erupts into battle as the GC attempt to retreat from the area.
You have defeated the first wave of the robotic force of the Golians.  However, the more deadly of the weapons are slower moving and are just now reaching the area.
A few of the GC have survived but with major wounds.  You quickly help them to get away before the Golians can mount another attack.

You fall back to a more secure area.  Prilit (GC): "Thanks to you I still live.  We had no idea they had constructed such a large number of robotic forces.  We have but a few such forces ourselves.  Hopefully we can defeat them and reclaim the Gridstone.

Suddenly the ground begins to shake.  Fearing another attack you prepare to fall back when...  Prilit: "Hold.  Those are our forces coming.  We are not without heavy equipment ourselves and I have had them called to the front.

With the aid of our walking war machines we should be able to defeat the Golians."  Your only previous experience with such machines was the scout you first encountered.  These new machines are even larger and look twice as deadly.
Prilit: "Now we shall see these Golians fry!  Ha Ha Ha!  Let us take a brief rest before we attack."
Prilit: "Attack!"  With his command the huge walking war machines march towards the Golian forces.
As you advance on the fortress a large robotic creature emerge.   It looks to be a large mechanical spider.  It carries a glowing object that looks to be the Gridstone.
It quickly shuffles toward the strange platform to the west of the fortress.  It deposits the Gridstone onto the platform where it begins to expand and glow with intense energy.
With the aid of the walking war machines you defeated the best the Golians had to throw at you.  You can now plan your assault on the fortress.
With the Gridstone in place the platform produces a huge amount of energy.  You watch on as a large underground panel opens to reveal some unknown device below.
A bright flash of light strikes out from the strange structure and strikes each of the walking war machines in turn.  They appear to loose all power.

The GC troops scramble to the machines in an attempt to get them powered back up.  At first it seem as if they are successful as they do begin to move again.  Prilit: "Good work men.  Without those weapons we would stand no chance!"

GC Trooper: "Sorry sir.  We did not do that. They just seem to come on again all by themselves!"  The war machines begin to power up as they turn to attack you.  Somehow the Golian have taken control of the war machines!
The robotic spider joins the battle.  At its feet are a whole host of Golian warriors.
Though not as large a force you also get a few more GC troops to aid you.
With the destruction of the Golian forces a GC trooper quickly rushes to the platform to grab the Gridstone.  As he touches the stone he is instantly vaporized.

Prilit: "Poor man.  I knew him well.  Somehow we need to destroy the fortress so we can power down the Gridstone matrix and retrieve it.  The main entrance to the fortress seems impregnable with all their robotic forces they now have.
We must find some other way inside if we are to ever defeat the Golians."
The area is crawling with Golian forces.
A strange building made from some metal you have never seen before.  The purpose of this structure is unknown.  The locking mechanism defies any attempt to crack or defeat magically.

Prilit: "This is nothing more than a triple bio-scan mechanical lock.  I can see why it would pose such a barrier to you and your magic but it is quite easy to defeat using this."  Prilit holds aloft a small card made of some shiny substance.
He places it inside a slot near the door and pulls it through quickly.  A small green light appears and you hear a click as the door lock releases.
Horns sound as you trigger some unknown alarm.  Up ahead you hear the sound of footsteps as well as mechanical units rushing to investigate.

Prilit: "Here!  This may be just what we need.  If I am correct I think this is an emergency access panel."  Prilit quickly taps a few colored lights on the panel and the warning horns go silent.  He taps a few more times and the lights go out.

Prilit: "That should do it.  I shunted the main power supply to a holding battery.  It will not take the Golians long to figure out what I have done and restore power.  Now is our chance to grab the Gridstone.  We must hurry."
Cormite quickly grabs 'The Geyser' and places it in a pouch on his belt.  Prilit: "The Gridstone must come with me.  Without it the Golians are sure to perish here and our task here is complete."
Cormite: "But what of our need of this relic.  Without it we can't hope to complete the Mithril Vault in time.  If Weston becomes a litch then our people as well as those of Winterhaven are doomed!"

Prilit: "Hmmm.  I must admit we do owe you a great debt for having helped us defeat the Golians.  This Mithril Vault of which you speak.  The purpose of this is to contain the one you call Weston while he is in this litch form correct?"

Cormite: "Yes.  There is a curse upon his soul that will cause him to become a litch when he dies.  We need that Vault to hold his evil litch form."   Prilit: "Perhaps I have a solution to both our problems.  As you know, our world does not have magic.

Not in any shape or form.  We are so far from any world that has a core that radiates magic that it fails utterly on our world.  Perhaps if we were to take Weston to our world, the curse would fail.  After all, the curse is based on magic is it not?"
Cormite: "By the gods that's right.  If your world does not have magic then the curse would be broken and Weston could die in peace.  We should return to our land right away.
I am sure Weston will be grateful beyond measure that he will not have to spend an eternity as a caged litch."  Prilit: "I have a mode of transportation that can return us to your land quickly."

King Cormite quickly shows Prilit where his land is located.  Though the journey is brief it is not nearly as quick as you would have hoped.  However, you do arrive in short order back to the warrens.
Weston is quickly summoned and you explain your play.  Weston is amazed to learn of these other worlds and of your struggle to regain 'The Geyser'
Weston: "This new learning amazes me!  If what you say is true about your world being void of magic then I have no doubt that the curse would be broken should you take me with you.

I only pray that your craft can take us there quickly as I fear I am very short for this world now.  We should leave right away."  Weston turns to you.  Weston: "Friends, I don't know how to thank you enough.

After we got and then lost "The Geyser" my hopes were all but dashed.  Now to find that not only will I not be a threat to others but may be free of the curse all together.  It is more than I could have hoped for."

Weston looks himself over.  Weston: "Well, I am about to travel to a new world.  One without magic.  That would make all these trappings useless.  I shall give them to you as a reward for your devotion to our cause."

Weston quickly removes the plethora of magical items he is wearing and gives them to you.  Weston: "Use them well my friends.  I hope they server you well as they have me."  Weston turns and walks with King Cormite and Prilit already deep in discussion.

A pair of dwarven warriors are facing a much larger force of shadow elves.  Without your aid these two were sure goners.

You happen upon a large scale engagement between the dwarves and elves.  Though there are a large number of dwarves they lack those that can cast magic and will be hard pressed to win.  That is until you showed up.
As you wipe your blades clean on the tunics of your foes a small dwarven child emerges from hiding near the back of the room.  Flanked by a pair of dwarven warriors the child approaches you.

Glinda: "Hail and well met my new found benefactors!"  This child looks to be quite young yet speaks with the dignity and grace more befitting a queen.  Glinda: "The puzzlement on your faces are plain and I shall explain.

Glinda: "I know it may seem difficult to believe but I assure you that I am who I say.  I have ruled over my peaceful island home for nearly all of those years.  However, as you can see.  Times are strange just now.

Hevritisis has always come to my aid in such times but she has been silent of late.  I fear a great disturbance for my most devote of priests have begun to age at an alarming rate.  By two guards that stand beside me.

These two guards who stand beside me.  They look to be in their 200s and yet, early this morning they could have easily have passed for no more than 100.  Everyone seems to be aging except for myself.  I seem to be growing younger and younger.
Soon I will be too young to use my protective magic and we will fall to these elves.  Hevritisis no longer speaks to me so I have no way of divining a cause or solution to our problem.

The only possible clue we have is a strange cave that appeared on the western edge of our island about the time our problems began.  Every patrol we have sent to investigate failed to return.  I am sure that the cause lies within the cave.
With these constant raids we dare not send a large force into the cave to investigate.  Perhaps a small group can infiltrate the area unseen and discover the cause.  Will you help us yet again?"
Glinda: "I beg of you to be quick.  At this rate all the warriors will be too old to fight in but a few days."

You spot a pair of harpies sleeping near a rock ledge overlooking the cave.  Behind them you can see the soft glow of a fire reflecting on the ceiling.  The muted sounds of more harpies arguing with some shadow elves can be heard as well.

You climb to the campsite above to search for clues.  You discover a small iron chest and easily crack it open to find a small jewel inside.

You search the campsite and discover the small iron chest.  You easily crack it open to find a small jewel inside.

The argument between the Harpies and Elves grows more intense.  So much so that one of the Harpies drops it's weapon to wave an accusing finger at the priestess.  The sudden movement triggers a reflex response in several of the Elves.

A battle erupts as the Elves and Harpies fight for possession of the chest.  Both sides are equally matched and they nearly wipe each other out.  The few wounded survivors are no match for you as you storm into camp.

The sole surviving elf of any rank is a wounded priestess.  You pump her for information but she dies before you can get anything of use.  The surviving harpies however are much less devote and easily crack.

Harpy: "Stop!  I will tell you all I know if you but release me.  I'm not privy to all that goes on here but what I do know is this.  Those foul elves search for five stones.  They are known as the 'Elemental Stones'.

Please, now let me go.  That is all I know, I swear."  Do you let the harpy go or do you slay him?
The harpy quickly limps to the edge of the cliff and leaps off.  It flutters away on a wounded wing.

Before you can slay the wretched creature it begs once again for you to spare him.  Harpy: "Stop I say!  I know more.  I will tell you all if you but let me go.  Gaz, our leader knew the location of yet another stone.  He told me where it was.

A family of dragons have it in their treasure horde.  We are not strong enough to slay these dragons.  That's why we were arguing with the elves.  They would have us attack the dragons without their aid.  The cowards!
I will draw you a map if you but release me."  Do you agree?

The harpy quickly draws you a map to a cavern just north of your current location.  You release the foul wretch as you study the map in earnest.  Knowing the prior location of these dragons will aid you in defeating them.
The foul harpy attempts to flee.  In your attempt to subdue him he falls victim to his previous wounds.
You find the cave as shown by the map from the harpy.  Knowing there are dragons inside, you can use a clever trick to lure them out into the open where your magic will be more effective.
Your ambush is most effective and you slay a half dozen of the great beasts before they know what hit them.
Searching the cavern you discover their treasure horde and an elemental stone!
This cavern is home to a large group of dragons.  An immense pile of treasure is piled near the back of their lair.
You slip past the guards unnoticed.
They continue to argue.  Do you wish to continue to wait or do you wish to attack now?

The argument continues.  The two large harpies holding the chest slowly back away to safeguard it.  One glances in your direction but does not seem to notice you... at first.  He quickly shouts a warning cry!

An abandoned village.  It looks to have been deserted in a rush.  The scars of battle are obvious from the dead bodies scattered about.  A few giant slugs are wandering about the village each bearing large wounds.
You hear the cry of a small child coming from one of the buildings on the other side of the village.  Do you rush to investigate?
As you near the small shack with the crying child you are suddenly surrounded by a large group of folk riding giant snails.  Snail Jockey: "You there!  Who are you and what are  you doing here?"
Snail Jockey: "Why, we are the ones who will slay you and let our mounts feed upon your rotting carcasses.  Attack!"

As you wipe your blades to remove blood and ichor of the snails, you hear whispering overhead.   You gaze up you see a large group of slug riders clinging to the ceiling directly above.  They appear to be talking about you.

They do not move to attack but are locked in discussion over what to do with about you.  Finally a group breaks away.  Their slug mounts ooze down a nearby wall and approach.  Palermole: "We thank you for what you attempted to do.

Though truth be told, that baby was a clever trick on our part to lure those damnable Snail Jockeys into a trap.  It's a common tactic on their part to attack a village and leave one small child alive.

When our patrols return to find the camp decimated they would rush in to rescue the child and thus fall prey to an yet another ambush.  However, we are wise to this trick and were in fact just about to ambush them.

You saved us the trouble and for that I thank you.  My name is Palermole.  My friends call me Mole for short and I now count you among my friends.  We have been at war with the Snail Jockeys for some time but they have been attacking in earnest of late.
