Mole: "Excellent!  I believe with the addition of those as mighty as you, we now have the tools and the talent to meet out justice."  Mole signals to have several large slugs brought forth to act as your mounts.

Mole: "My original company was only 300 riders and handlers.  However, we brought with us hundreds of spare mounts for those mercenaries we hired on the way.  We are now a formidable force.  May the blessing of Vicklin smile upon us all!"

You travel by Moles side as you journey towards Snelvista.  He quickly learns of your vast deeds and heroics.  Mole: "My friends, I would be remiss in my duties to not place you higher in the ranks of our army.

It's obvious to me that you are no strangers to combat.  Though much of our force are seasoned combatants they lack a certain sense of focus and direction.  I shall make each of you captains in our army.

As such, should you survive the battle you would each be entitled to a much larger payment and share of the spoils."  Mole assigns each of your party a contingent of mercenaries as well as a few of his best Slug Knights.

After several days travel you find yourself on the outskirts of Snelvista.  Before each of you takes your force and moves to encircle the city Mole gives you one final set of instructions.  Mole: "Do not underestimate these vermin.

They have enslaved many beasts of the underworld and will not hesitate to use them against us in battle.  Some of which I am sure even I have never encountered before.  Let Vicklin smile upon us all."
Each member of your party makes ready to attack.  Finally Mole gives the signal and the city is beset by hundreds of marauding bands.  Several of which are under your direct command.
As battles rage on around you,  another of your party is thrust into the fray!
Mole: "Very well.  I don't blame you.  You are obviously mighty folk and may not wish to stoop to being simple mercenaries.  I bid you farewell and once again thank you for your help thus far.
As those defending Snelvista fall back into a defensive knot near the center of the city, your entire group presses to wipe them out.
A few of those enslaved by Snelvista are forced to join its defense.
Having smashed the core of the defending force, those that remain break and run.  It was a battle of total carnage and one hard fought by both sides.  Those who survive gain an extra level.

Mole rushes up to you with a wide grin on his face.  Mole: "Well fought my friends!  Their forces are broken and scattered.  I would imagine it will be sometime before they can rebuild and cause us any more trouble.

Later that evening, after much needed rest Mole seeks you out.  Mole: "Well my friends.  It's time to settle our great debt to you.  You were worth ten times you weight in gold in today's battle.

Mole: "Hmmmm.  Not quite sure what that thing is.  We came upon it while clearing out a large building near the center of Snelvista.  I don't know if I would feel right if that's all you took.  Please, take it and choose something else as well."
Mole: "Great wealth is what you seek.  By all means.  Take the entire chest.  You have earned it and more!"

Mole: "Farewell my friends.  I must attend to paying the others before I make ready to return home in victory.  I would ask you to return with us in triumph but I see that you are anxious to get on with your own lives."
Mole: "You are wise my friends.  My companion Melbrite is the most powerful mage in our entire kingdom.  His gift will be something I am sure you will find most useful."

Mole: "Ah!  A good choice.  Most of those items were taken as loot from a large building near the center of town.  I'm told they appear to be fairly powerful magical items but I am a man true to his word.  They are yours."

This boat seems to be in fine shape.  It gives you a way to travel upon the back of the 'Hells Serpent'  It must have been captained by a powerful wizard at one time.  You find a secret compartment underneath the captains bunk.

Inside you find a bevy of magic items as well as a strange elemental stone unlike any you have seen before.

A huge Golian giant is literally ripping the roof off this building.  This giant is easily 7 feet taller than any other giant you have ever seen.  Two elven priestesses are driving the huge giant to tear the roof off.
Elven Priestess: "Brim!  Tear that roof off now!  I don't care if they are cutting your fingers!  Peel that roof off and pluck them out so we can kill them!"

You watch in horror as the giant succeeded in tearing the roof from the building.  His fingers are dripping blood as the dwarves inside have slashed at his hands.  Brim reaches inside and pulls out a handful of dwarves.

As you prepare to leave the village you see a huge number of Golian giants to the north.  One of them spots you and shouts, "Those damn elves have taken dad prisoner again!"

The roof of this hut has been torn away.  Inside you see a dead dwarven family.

You spot a large structure up ahead.  The smell of rotting fish fills the air.  The water just in front of you is unnaturally turbulent.  A few large fins crest the water then sink away.  Something is swimming beneath the surface.
Behind you the water erupts into a foaming mass.  Strange sea creatures try to catch you.  However you were too quick for them and you got away.
As you move slowly across the water you see masses of tiny air bubbles begin to float up about you.  Whatever is living in the water knows your there and attacks!
A small humanoid pokes its head from the building and waves to you.  He yells "Come on!  You can make it.  But you have to be real fast!"
Nearly out of breath you quickly pick up the pace and make it to shore without further attacks.

The small humanoid is in fact a gnome.  Lane: "Hullooo dare!  I am Lane.   Sure glad to see you.  I have been trapped here for some time now and I am almost out of supplies.  I built this dwelling nearly 300 sleeps ago but now I can't get out.

I see you made it here.  You have to be fast to get past them vermin in the river.  My short stumpy legs just can't carry me fast enough.  I came out here to get away from all the hustle and bustle of Snelflinbig.  That's the town where I use to live."
You try to interrupt, but the fast talking gnome will have none of it.  Like most gnomes Lanes mind is working in overdrive and you literally have to slap a hand over his mouth to get a word in.

Ramius: "Lane,  what gives with those creatures in the lake?  How did you get here and build this hut if they were there?"  Lane: "They were not there when I moved in you silly vark!  Now just you listen and let Lane finish his tale!

After I built this place those fish men showed up.  At first I did not mind as they will not come this far out of the water so I am safe as long as I stay here.  I was happy as a clam tending my mushroom patch till it happened."
Ramius: "It?  What It?"  Lane: "My shrooms started to change.  One day I had a nice little crop on the north end of the field, the next day they would all be on the south side.
At first I didn't know what to make of it but what did I care.  As long as they continued to grow bigger and bigger I was happy.  However, things got stranger and stranger.

One day I was in the field tending my favorite Flat Top Vodalias, that's a kind of mushroom.  Well, all of a sudden a Speckled Humphrite in the next row just moved over and seemed to eat it.  I never saw anything like it.
Now the whole field is nothing but these mushroom eating things and I have no food left.  Seems I was doomed to starve to death until you showed up.

Lane: "Hmmmm.  Tis tempting, but I must decline.  I have made this my home and I do so wish to stay.  However, if you would be so kind as to help me clear my fields and return them to good order I will give you this!"

Lane holds before you a small broach.  Lane: "I found this when I was digging in the field.  I'm quite certain it's magical but I have no use for such things.  I'm sure it's quite valuable but I will let you have it if you help me.  Do you agree?"
Lane frowns and becomes very angry with you.  Lane: "Very well then!  I shall have to ask you to leave as I do like to keep to myself.  Good day to you!"

Lane: "Excellent!  Just to the north you will find my fields.  They are crawling with these... things.  I managed to kill one or two small ones but they just keep coming back.  I'm at a loss.  I do hope you can clear them away for me."
As you tromp around the field some of the mushrooms rise up and attack.  There seems to be no end to them.  For every one you strike down another just takes it's place!
You grab each tiny mushroom and pull it from the ground and toss it onto a bonfire.  Though not very loud you can hear the small mushrooms shriek as you toss them on the fire.   Creepy!

Lane: "Burned em did ya!  Ha!  I never thought of that.  I tried just about everything I could think of but never tried to burn em."  Lane hands you the broach.  Lane: "Not sure what it is, seems magical but also seems broke.

I'm pretty good at fixing things but when it comes to magic I steer clear.  Had a friend once who was turned into a varsk when he was messing with a magic wand.  Never did find a way to change him back."

Inside this shallow cave you see a large group of shrieks growing from a moldy lump near a damp corner.  They appear to be feeding off the lump.  Whatever it was, it is nothing but fertilizer for these foul plants now.  Do you attack?

You notice something of interest coming from the lump the Shrieks were feeding on.  It appears to be the body of a dead gnome.  As you dig through the pile you find nothing of value except a small broken clasp.
You fit the broken clasp to the end of the broach.  A blinding flash assaults your eyes.  When the spots clear you see that the clasp has fused to the broach making it whole again.
Lane: "Well, seems that I can go on living my life as I please thanks to you.  I don't want to seem rude but I do like to keep to myself as much as I can.

If your interested, I will show you how to get to my former city of Snelflinbig in exchange for that broach I just gave you.  Deal?"  Do you trade back the broach in exchange for a map to Snelflinbig?
Lane: "Very well then, I bid you good day and ask you to move along.  I have much work to do in getting my fields back in shape and ready for planting."

Lane: "Well, lets see now.  As I recall..." Lane scratches out a crude map showing you the way to Snelflinbig and hands it to you.  Lane: "Odds are you sailed right past it on your way here.  It's hard to find and Snelflinbig likes it that way."

Lane: "Hmmmm.  I don't know if I care to pay the price.  However, I see that I have little choice and you strike a hard bargain.  I will give all the money I have if you rid my fields of those vermin.  How does that sound?"
Lane: "Well, I said I would give you all my wealth and so I will."  Lane holds up a sack stuffed with gems.  It would seem he is true to his word.
Your water based magic allows you to meld with the water.  As you try to touch the gem it now feels as solid as granite.  You can easily grasp the stone and remove it from the pool of water.
You enter what was at one time a small shop.  Most of the items have been looted by the Golian Giants.  You hear sobbing coming from beneath a pile of old sacks near the corner.
You clear away the sacks to find the shopkeeper clutching a small child who has been killed in the raid.  Try as you might you can't get the attention of the shopkeeper.

You lend aid to the small child.  The healing powers of magic are strong and soon the child open its eyes.  The shopkeeper is so overjoyed that he can hardly speak.  Gwem: "By da gods ye have done it!  Me thinkin Sliva be a goner for sure!"

Still too choked up to speak clearly the shopkeeper hands you a small key and points to a blank spot on the far wall.  You look closely to find a small keyhole where none should be.  You insert the key and a small panel open up.

Inside you see a dusty tomb.  The shopkeeper motions you to take the ancient relic as a gift for your aid.  Gwem: "Please, take it.  It's all I have left to offer ye for your help.  I must make haste and try to get away before more Golians come.

They have driven nearly everybody out but I refused to leave.  When Sliva was hurt I cursed myself for not leaving sooner.  I will not make that same mistake twice."  Gwem turns and bolts out the door with Sliva tucked under both arms.
Who will read this book?
Energy courses through your muscles.  You move with a quickness and grace beyond your normal ability.  This character gains 1 full attack per round in combat.
Who will drink this potion?
You feel a tingle run through your body.  You feel more robust than ever before!  You have gained 30 points of stamina permanently!
You enter a shop.  The shopkeeper has heard of your arrival and does not look to be pleased with your presence in his city.

Piercing shrieks echo from overhead.  As you search the darkness for signs of an ambush you see nothing but the cold waves of the Hells Serpent.  You continue your journey but can't escape the feeling your being watched.
You find another ship jammed in the rocks.  The deck is caked with blood and entrails of shadow elven warriors.  Do you wish to pull along side the deserted craft?
The gentle splash of waves upon the hull of the derelict vessel is calming to the nerves.  As you stalk the deck of the ghost ship you find strange fibers embedded in the wounds of the elven victims.
Suddenly you hear the trumpeting calls of a large creature rising from beneath the boats hull.
A small cavern with a few scaly dwellers.  They are not pleased to see you.
You see a small grotto up ahead.  A lone shadow elf stalks the area.  She seems to be either talking to herself or praying to her unholy god.

As you enter the grotto she quickly sees you but does not react in a hostile manner.  It's as if she almost invites you to kill her.  Wealvin: "Come forward, I see that you mean me no harm and I for one have no ill feelings toward you."

You approach with caution.  Shadow Elves are rarely of a mild temperament but it's not unheard of.  Ramius: "What's your name and if you don't mind my asking, what are you doing here all alone so far from any homeland you may call your own?"

Wealvin: "I'm Wealvin and I call no land my home.  I have been banished here by the ilk that were once my people.  Once I was a great priestess but now I'm but a vagabond of the deep.  I have forsaken the ways of my people and they have forsaken me.

Though not well known, many of my people would throw off the yokes of slavery we place upon others.  I for one could not, and indeed will not continue to enslave those we should rightfully call our neighbors and friends.
You have found a true rarity, a shadow elf who would treat other races as equals.  Do you invite her to join your band?

Wealvin: "If you will have me then I would gladly go with you.  I'm not one for the lonely life of a hermit."  Wealvin rushes to the nearby well she has constructed and retrieves a small sack coated in fish oil.
Wealvin: "I took this from my temple before I was banish.  If they knew I had it in my possession they would have slain me for heresy.  I give it to you gladly as a gift of friendship."
Wealvin: "I often thought of drinking it myself but I could never bring myself to use that which was made in such an evil way."  Ramius: "How was this potion constructed?"

Wealvin: "The life force of nearly a dozen slaves were drained to make this potion.  All of them goblin children of no more than a few years of age.  You may use it as you like, but I will have no more of it.  Let us leave for I weary of this place."
Wealvin: "You are like all the others and are not fit to live!"
You find a small rope buried in the crusty soil used to construct this crude well.  You pull on it to reveal a small leather sack coated in fish oil.  Inside you find a small vial.
You find nothing but ordinary supplies and a small diary.  It has little of interest.
Once again you hear the cry of something overhead.  This time you hear the flapping of wings.  High overhead you see large flying creatures begin to dive upon you.
This area of the river is jealously guarded.
You land on this small island only to discover that it's a breeding ground!  One that's in high demand by the lower orders of life common in this area.
You find yourself standing on the shore of the small island in the middle of the lake.
The lake is populated with many creatures that consider you but a tasty morsel!
This hut has been abandoned.
A small family of dwarves are sitting at a mushroom stump table.  They are playing a rather odd game involving a large bone, three small sticks and a dozen or more polished stones.
The father tosses the stones and sticks on the table.  He then tries to separate the red stone using the large bone without touching any of the sticks.

He knocks a stick and it brings a roar of glee from the rest of the family!  Kligor: "Bah!  Dis game be for young folk.  Not for grown folk!"  He smirks as he pushes the sticks and stones to the next player.
His children poke his arm as they chant "Sticks and stones may break our bones but names will never hurt me!"  Do you wish to announce yourself to the occupied family?

Kligor: "Who be you and what are you doing skulking about our house!"  Ramius: "Sorry for the interruption, but we were just curious as to the nature of this small cottage in the middle of this lake.  Why do you live way out here?"

Kligor: "Because it be safe, dat's why!  What kind of a fool da ya tink I be?  All the other farms be destroyed already.  We be the last one as da water keeps us safe."  Ramius: "What destroyed the other farms?"

Kligor: "Some sort of giant snake beasts.  They have large wings and can tear a farm apart in seconds.  Don't know what they be.  Never seen em before and don't care to see em again.  They won't fly over water though.
Seems dey be scared of da water as they never come close to this island.  Whatever da reason, tis good enough for me.  Keeps me family safe as long as I stay out here.
This small patch of farmland seems different than any you have seen in the past.  A strange aroma that nearly makes you retch comes from the ground.

The putrid smell of the soil is nearly more than you can stand.  Whatever is used to fertilize this section of the field, it's most foul.  You dig further and find a large clump of hair rotting beneath the surface.
This farm has been destroyed.  The buildings have been demolished and abandoned.
This appears to be the farmers barge.  He must use it to get his crops inland.
As you continue to excavate you find the rotting corpse of a large beast buried here.
You pull a portion of the carcass free.
You see a large group of snake-like creatures in the distance.  You wish to engage them in battle?

Kligor: "Peeeuuuuu!  What ya got der?"  You hold the strange object before Kligor and tell him you found it buried in the soil.  Kligor: "Dat be nuttin but a piece of a wooly beast!  I found a few dead ones near the shore a few weeks back.

I floated it out here and buried it in the fields to make my crop grow.  What do you want with it?"  Ramius: "It might have something to do with why those creatures won't attack your farm.  We shall see."
Kligor: "Hmmmm, if dat be the case then I guess I am lucky to have em stinkin up the place.  Your welcome to that piece if you please.  Good day to ya."

You pull out the rotting piece of Wooly Beast and wave it before you.  The pungent smell assails the acute smell of the Ulrick Snakes.  They turn in fear thinking that a wooly beast may be in the area.
There are just too many Ulrick Snakes.  Another group steps up to take the place of those you have just slain.  They are guarding the area to their rear with their lives.
You see a group of Ulrick Snake destroying a nearby farm.  Several of them see you and attack!

The ground begins to shake as large beasts emerge from a cave to the west.  The Ulrick Snakes cease their attack as they spot the large Wooly Beasts emerging from the cave.  Some snakes turn and flee in terror at the sight of the Wooly Beasts.
One snake gets too close to its huge tusks.  The Wooly Beast shakes the Ulrick Snake like a rag doll before tossing it to the ground.
The Wooly Beasts are so huge that they do not even see you as a threat.  Many of the Ulrick Snakes flee.

The Ulrick Snakes appear to be justified in being deathly afraid of Wooly Beasts.  The beasts appear to be the only animal in the area that are more than a match for Ulrick Snakes.  Just the smell of the Wooly Beasts seemed to panic the snakes.
The cave is littered with the bones of Ulrick Snakes.  A few Wooly Beasts loiter about the area but do not see you as a threat and do not pay you a second look.
The smell of this cave reminds you of the Wooly Beast carcass you dug up in the farmers field.
The dreadful smell reminds you of the cavern that was home to the Wooly Beasts. It was almost as if the scent alone was enough to drive the Ulrick Snakes into a panic.
Kligor gives you a ride back to shore and bids you farewell.
You enter a dwarven temple.
A creaky door leads to a well stocked shop.

A small but comfortable tavern.  It's known as 'The Inn of the Flickering Flame'  It's easy to see how it got its name.  Every square inch of the walls is covered with burning torches.  The smell of burning pitch is heavy in the air.
You overhear: "Aye, truth be told, I think that crazy farmer on that island is the cause of the problems.  Those damnable beasts never seem to bother him!"

You overhear: "Been a whole pack of those crazy snakes to the south of town for as long as I can remember.  They never bothered us too much until late.  Something has them all stirred up, that's for sure."

You overhear: "Palami told me that he was going to try and sneak past them damn snakes and see what's beyond.  He heard from a sage that they were set there to guard an ancient castle full of treasure."
You overhear: "I'm packing it in Hevron.  Me dad says there be a whole tribe of ogres coming to destroy the town.  We be getting out of here before they show."
You overhear: "Some nosy adventurer types been trying to listen in on conversations.  I would be careful of what ye say if I were ye."
You overhear: "Captain Glavum has not heard word from our kin at Silver Peak for some time now.  Gots him all worried."
You overhear: "Shhhh.  We be splittin up the loot in half an hour.  Meet me just west of the main gate and I will take you to where we got the goods hid."
Barkeep: "Mmmm.  You be all full o questions are ya.  Most folk just mind their own affairs.  I suggest you do the same."

Barkeep: "Talk been going around about how a whole clan of ogres were driven out of their homes by a powerful wizard.  Word has it that they blame us somehow and mean to attack the town.  Bah!  Just rumors says I."
Barkeep: "If it be adventure you be lookin for, then come with me."  Do you follow the barkeep?
The crowd roars in laughter at your tale.  Most think your a bunch of braggarts and would tell you so to your face... if they could stop laughing at you.

He takes you to a small stairwell.  Barkeep: "Down that way be a beast I never seen the likes of before.  Nearly killed me on two separate occasions.  I have not been able to go down there for over three weeks now.

The town militia sent a few troops in after it but they never came back.  They say they can't risk the lives of any  more troops to search for them.  I would be just as happy to lock the door and let it rot down there but all me ale be down there.
I had some extra ale in some barrels out back but that's nearly gone.  Once I run out, so will my customers.  If you be as brave as you say, then have a go at that critter down below."
Lights out!
The barkeep said there was only one creature but you see two!  They look similar to vermin you have battled in the past.  This should be easy!
Having slain the beast it explodes into a cloud of vapor.  Those that breath in the noxious vapor must Save Vs. Chemical or have their stamina reduced by 10 permanently!
You ascend the steps to the tavern above.
The smell of death and rot is heavy in the air as you descend into the damp cellar below the tavern.
Locked!  The barkeep eyes you closely.  You find it wise to back away from the door to avoid further suspicion.
A drunken patron.  They make it clear they don't care for your company.
Maid: "Helloo!  If you need anything just ask.  Otherwise if you want to get a drink right away you can ask the barkeep in the corner."
A pair of dead guards.  These must have been the two sent down here to ferret out the creature.  They died without even having drawn steel.
The body of a dead thief.  He was good enough to get past the locked door above but fell prey to these creatures just the same.
You must Save Vs. Knowledge.  If you succeed you will gain the ability to cast one additional spell per round in combat.
Who will read the book?  (Choose A Spell Caster)
Success!  You gain the ability to cast one more spell per round in combat.
Failed!
Barkeep: "I don't believe my eyes!  You met with those critters, er, critter and lived to tell about it!"  Ramius: "You said it the first time brother, CRITTERS.  There was two and you knew that!"

Barkeep: "Now don't go blaming me.  I figured a tough lot such as yourselves could handle two as easily as one.  No harm done.  I tell you what.  Just to show you I have no hard feelings take this.  It shows how to sneak into the hall of commons."
The gate is heavily guarded and you are not allowed into the hall of commons.  Try as you might you just can't talk you way in.
You find a secret passage.

This passage shows signs of recent excavation.  It can't be more than a week or two old.  The barkeep said he has not been down here in over three weeks.  That can only mean that somebody is tunneling down here without his knowledge.
The passageway splits into two directions.  You spot a small group of humanoids working in the distance.  They appear to be shoring up the walls.  Do you wish to move closer?
You spot a work crew of small reptilian creatures.  Overlording over them are a patrol of shadow elves.
The noise has alerted another work crew from further down the tunnel.
You make your attempt to sneak past.  If you fail to sneak past you will be forced to do battle.

You tell the guards about the trickery planned by the shadow elves and of the tunneling that is going on beneath their very feet.  Gate Guard: "Hmmmmm, this must be reported right away.  Let them pass!"  They wave you through.
This portion of the tunnel has caved in.  Work has stopped and the area is clear of workers.  The smell of decomposing bodies from beneath the rubble is strong.
Scattered about are the corpses of many dead Thrultain workers and one dead shadow elf.  The workers have little of value but the dead elf has one item of interest.
This characters base movement is increased by four points.  Permanently!

You see a small shaft leading down.  You contemplate where it might lead.  Shortly after you hear the hissing sounds of Thrultain laborers coming from below.  Do you wish to ambush the work crew as they exit the tunnel or collapse the tunnel in upon them?
Ambush Them
Collapse The Tunnel
The tunnel collapses upon the arriving Thrultain work crew.  You hear screams and muffled cries as they suffocate in the damp soil.

You hear more Thrultain coming up the tunnel.  A wounded Thrultain attempts to climb down the tunnel to safety.  In its weakened state it accidentally kicks a supporting member of the tunnel entrance.
You see a group of massive giants in the distance.  Do you attack?

You enter a sweltering cave.  Steam rises from cracks in the cavern floor.  Just a few feet outside the cave entrance it's a frozen wasteland.  Inside it's sub tropical.  Large wet foot prints are all about the entrance to this cavern.
You see a large group of dragons and giants camped near a cool corner of the cave.  Do you approach?
A large snow giant pushes his way to the front to confront you.  Galarn: "You there!  Are you little people responsible for this oppressive heat!"  How do you answer?
Galarn: "Then let us be done with it as I shall slay you all now!"

Galarn: "Have you any knowledge of how these accursed cracks have come to be.  They belch forth a heat and stench that I can't bare.  This has the stink of magic upon it.  You had better tell me all you know."  Do you tell your story or evade the truth?
Tell what you know
Evade the truth
Galarn: "As I suspected.  I feel you are more at fault than you would care to admit."

Galarn: "As I suspected.  You do not look to have the power to do such as this in any case.  However, those of your puny size may have some use for me.  I have a task for those such as you and the reward would be handsome indeed.  Interested?
Galarn: "Very well then.  If you will not work for me, you will not work for anyone!"

Galarn: "I have a rival I wish to be rid of.  However, the nature of my rival makes it impossible for me to do the job myself.  My rival you see is my brother, Malicus.  If  you could assassinate Malicus then I could take control of his lands.
Lands which are free of this accursed heat.  Do me this favor and I shall in return give you a bauble that I am sure you could use.  Is it a deal?"

Take this map.  It will show you how to reach the kingdom of my brother Malicus.  Slay him quickly and then return for your reward.  Take care not to fall into his hands or betray our dealings in this matter.

If he should discover it is I behind this plot it would be the end of me... and you.  One thing more.  His realm is guarded by a powerful glyph of warding.  To pass this ward you must utter the command word 'Daggerfall'."
As you pass over the glyph of warding it pushes you back.
You clearly state the magical world of passing, "Daggerfall" and the glyph pulsates for a moment in response.

A tall spire reaching nearly 200 feet overhead.  Obviously made by giants, this huge structure would be a fortress by human standards.  For giants it's but a lookout post.  You find it unmanned at the time which is odd indeed.
You ascend the tower to the topmost ramparts.   To the northeast you see a cave along a rocky shoreline.  To the south you see a large snow covered fortress.

Using a simple but clever trick you throw your voice to another part of the valley.  The blind Wooly Beasts believe you to be elsewhere and trudge off towards the noice.  This gives you enough time to dash past them.
A number of blind Wooly Beasts are chained to a pair of large anchors.  Though they can't see you, they have excellent hearing and can still attack.  They seem capable of tracking you by sound alone.
The massive crush of bodies forces you back the way you came to avoid being trampled.
A quaint magic shop.  It has little to offer of any major magical power but the prices are very good.
A small warehouse.  The man who runs it allows you to store items here for a small fee.
A small shop that appears to be closed.  A sign on the door reads 'Gone Fishin'.  Just how long that is it does not say.
You see a locked door.  It's a lock unlike any you have ever seen and may well prove to be impossible to bypass without the key.
You detect no sign of a trap.
You have triggered a trap!
You find the lock is trapped.  This has got to be one of the most complex traps you have ever seen.
Inside you find a well stocked shop and nobody to mind the store.
Failure has a high price!
This grave has been dug up.  The skeletal remains have been pulled from the grave.  The looters were in search of a ring as the skeleton is complete minus one missing finger.
You find a skeletal finger with a shining ring.
You are spotted breaking into the shop.  A local summons the nearest patrol.
Your careless maneuver cost you some victory points.  The shop is locked and put under guard until the shopkeeper returns.
An old ship is anchored in the bay.  The thick layer of barnacles betray its age.  It does not look to have moved in many years.  Did you want to search below decks?
As you move below decks your nostrils become privy to a less than pleasing odor.  Garbage and refuse are piled waist high.  You pick your way among the trash and head for the captains cabin.
As you move through the filthy hallway you must Save Vs. Vitality or contract a disease.
Out from the filth and muck comes some disease ridden scavengers!

During the melee you have tipped over a large pile of refuse.  A dead demon has been exposed.  The demon must have recently fallen victim to these same vermin.  Perched upon the rafters above is a large Raven.
A long dark cavern retreats into the mountainside.  You feel a rush of air pouring out of the cave mouth.  It must have another entrance on the other side of this mountain.
You stumble upon a large nest of Basilisks near the center of the cavern.  They spot you as well but seem unwilling to attack you.  Do you attack or backup?
Attack
Backup

Near the center of the cave you see a large clutch of eggs.  Most have been trampled in the melee.  However, a few are just now hatching.  You take the young Basilisks into your care.  They could be potent allies in battle.

You spot a small group of rock giants having some fun.  They are pulling massive boulders from the shoreline and hurling them into the sea.  They are laughing and jesting like a bunch of drunken sailors.

One spots you and gives you a friendly wave.  You move closer for a better look.  For the most party they seem quite friendly.  However,  it could be a trick to lure you closer.  Do you wish to attack or try and befriend them?
For the most part they seem quite friendly.  However, it may be a trick to lure you closer.  Do you wish to attack or try and befriend them?
Attack
Make Friends

Soon you are laughing as loudly as the giants as you become good friends.  They invite you to join in the fun and toss some boulders into the sea.  You take one look at the massive rocks and frown.  The giants erupt in more laughter.

Maglock: "Ha Ha Ha!  Don't despair my small friends.  Tis a game we like to play but I fear it's not one for you.  Till we meet again."  Maglock and his friends stroll down the shoreline in search of more rocks.
As you eye the large boulders with despair you hear your new friend calling to you in the distance.  Maglock: "Hail friends!  I see you wish to try tossing a few rocks after all.  Ha Ha Ha Ha!"

Maglock: "Step aside and watch how far I can throw these pebbles."  Maglock bends down and wrenches a huge boulder from the shoreline.  With thick corded muscles he hurls it onto the riverbank.   It lands with a resounding thud.

With a grin on his face he continues to pluck boulders from the stream until there are none left.  Maglock: "Not bad eh!   It's been good to see you again but I was on my way home.  I am very late and have to rush.  Farewell my friends."

The fortress seems unguarded.  The tracks of snow giants litter the ground in all directions.  You ponder the dangers that may lay before you when a loud warning horn sounds from a rocky crag to the north.

You are stunned to see a large snow giant patrol racing towards you from the north.  They have weapons raised and are shouting war cries.  There is precious little real estate to use for cover.  Do you want to stand your ground or dash inside?
Stand and fight
Bolt for the castle
The patrol swarms over you like a pack of angry wolves!
You dash for the castle door.  The door to the fortress is a massive gate.  The gate is much too large to open easily.
You must make a Save vs. Brawn at a -2 penalty to open the massive door.  Who will try to pull the door open?
You manage to pry the gate open just wide enough to allow you to slip inside.  Once inside you put your shoulder to the door and force it shut.  You slam the locking post into place.
You failed to get the door open in time.  The patrol swarms over you like a pack of angry wolves!

Many small puddles of water are scattered about the entrance.  A large number of wet cloaks are hanging to dry.  A large snow giant stands nearby as you enter.  Snow Giant: "You there!  Who be you and why be you here?"
You are so smart and so slick.   You think up a lie and you think it up quick!
Yancy: "Galarn!  That snake has only one order of business.  If you be counted among his lackeys then we do indeed welcome you.  Tis always best to confront your enemies directly."
The inside of this fortress is nothing but one huge hall.  A few mighty pillars keep the massive roof from collapsing.

You come face to face with Malicus.  He stares at  you  curiously.   Malicus: "So, my brother would send you to do his dirty work would he.  No matter.  You made the right choice in telling me of his scheme.
He has been after my land for some time now.  Ever since our father passed on and left me the southern region.  He has managed his inheritance poorly and already his land is a stark wasteland.
If left up to him, the entire region would be a barren waste within a few years.  I am sure he promised you much.  Do not fear that you have missed out on any reward by telling me the truth.

Galarn is a notorious liar.  I would stake my life that he would have tried to slay you the moment you returned.  He would rather commit murder than to pay you whatever fee he promised.  I tire of his attempts to topple me and usurp my lands.
I intend to put a stop to his foul deeds once and for all.  You are in a unique position to aid me in this.  I do not wish to kill him but would prefer to capture him and place him on trial.

He had our younger sister killed when she spoke against him.  Though I have no hard proof of such, I know it in my heart.  If you aid me in bringing him to justice I am sure we could come to an agreement that would make us both happy.  Do you agree?"

Malicus: "Very well.  This is my plan.  You shall return to Galarn and claim to have slain me.  Once he hears I am dead he will surely attempt to kill you.  He will not do it right away as it's not in his nature to put himself in harms way.

He will pay you your fee and send you on your way.  Later when you make camp you will more than likely be ambushed.  However, it is my hope to have him in custody by then.  His desire for control of my lands is so strong

I dare say he will set off to claim them immediately.  I and a group of my best warriors will wait in ambush.  When he turns south you should do the same and prevent him from escaping.  When the battle turns against him he will surely try to flee.

When he does you shall be there to capture him and hold him until I can arrive.  If all goes as planned you shall keep whatever reward he has given you plus I will add to it myself.  We should be off and set our trap."

You place the Book of Turanians onto the chest of the skeletal figure.  A ghostly voice seems to seep from the very walls.  Ghost: "Brother... You have returned.  Our studies of this ancient vault was almost complete when you left.

You left me here to complete the work even though you knew the dangers.  With only our loyal servant Cherbourg to aid me we were unable to avoid the denizens of this place for long.  I was gravely wounded and I fee that Cherbourg will soon be all alone.

I sent you this tomb as an example of the fine works we could discover here but you never came back.  Brother... Brother... Why do you not answer me?"  A chill runs up your spine as you consider your options.  If this apparition should turn hostile...
there is little telling what it may do.  What do you say?

Ghost: "What!  How is it you came by this tomb?  I had a copy sent to my brother.  The only other copy should be right here.... hey!  Where is it.  Better yet.  Where am I?  I don't seem to be here.  What is going on here?"
You inform the ghost of his nether worldly self.  Ghost: "My god!  Can this be?  What year is this?  Where am I?  Who are you?  How did you get here?  Why are you here?  Did you do this?"

With each passing second the ghost grows more angry and frustrated with his inability to grasp the fact that he is dead.  Suddenly you see a white glow engulf the room.  Ghost: "You have done this to me!  Don't deny it!  I shall see you dead!"

As the wispy form of Yemire the Ghost begins to fade it speaks one last time.  Yemire: "Thank you... I think."  The Book of Turanians slowly begins to fade as well.  However, a single page remains behind and glows with an a eerie radiance.
Who shall attempt to read the paper?

A see a quick flair of light and a thunder crack booms in your ear.  Though you can't be sure, you think you hear a voice mixed in with the thunderclap.  Voice: "Thank  you... I think."   You gain +15 to your Armor Rating.
Ghost: "Well, I am very busy just now.  I have much research to complete before my brother arrives.  Now if you will excuse me I must be going."   The ghostly voice fades.
Ghost: "What do you mean, 'Lies before you a corpse.  Do I look like a .... wait one moment.  What is this?  Where is my body?  Have you turned me invisible?"
The form of Yemire the ghost seems to regain strength at an incredible pace.  He feeds off his own rage to renew his power.
An ancient tomb that is now an infested with those that make meals from such as you.
You comb through the dead bodies and refuse that is piled high in this room and find a few dead adventurers.  Their equipment may be of some use.

You enter the room with a stare of amazement upon your face.  The room appears to be well tailored for life under ground.  Fresh provisions are stacked in the corner.  A large bed and living quarters appear to be set up as well.
Two large creatures dressed in evil looking gear take immediate offense at your intrusion.  Just who or what they are and why they are hidden here in this remote location is unknown.
A large lever.  Do you wish to throw it?
Hmmmmmmm
A dirty well.  It's foul with the stink of some unknown poison.

A small goblin encampment.  They do not like visitors and defend it with their lives.  Goblin Leader: "You murdering scum!  Can't you just leave us be!  First the water now our very lives.  Well no more!"
Inside this sweltering hut you see several sick goblin children.  A few goblin women are among them but they also look ill.
You pour a vial of antidote into the well.  Soon the water is purified enough to drink.  However, the people of this village are still deathly ill from the water they have already drunk.

You search out a survivor of the battle to interrogate him.  Wounded Goblin: "Ughhh!  So thirsty.  Water, water please!"  You give the wounded goblin a drink of fresh water.  Wounded Goblin: "Your not with them are you?  With the invaders I mean."
You ease the fears of this wounded goblin who is no more than a boy really.  You soon discover that the villages well was poisoned by another clan of goblins to the south.

Wounded Goblin: "We would not pay tribute to that fat pig Greshim of the clan Hollowtooth.  They came into the village and poisoned our water.  Before we know what they did most of our children and women had already drank the water.

Now Greshim says that if we do not pay tribute that he will not give us the antidote.  However, times are so bad that we have nothing left to give in tribute so I fear we are doomed.  We are not strong enough to defeat him ourselves."
What precious few warriors we had are now dead or dying from the poison.  Now you have sealed our fate by slaying the few of us remaining.  We are doomed for sure."  Do you offer to help the village?
Wounded Goblin: "Please hurry.  We will not last long without water.  Even now our people begin to die of  thirst and that accursed poison."
You have 5 days past midnight to help the Goblin people.  Any longer than that and they will be beyond any aid you can lend.
Your time to save the goblin village has expired.  The goblins are doomed and beyond any aid you could now lend.  Each character looses 5000 prestige points.
You have purified the village well and cured the people of their poison.  You are local heroes!  You each gain a level.
You stand at the gate of a massive goblin city.  In all your days you have never seen such a large city of goblin kind.  Rarely are they organized enough to build so many dwellings in location.
Even with the large size of this city it is still in the typical goblin fashion.  No roads and huts packed so tight as to be almost on top of each other.

At the gate is a large force of heavily armed goblins.   Most appear to be part of a full time militia.  Again, something unheard of in the goblin world.  Most villages have a few warriors but most have other duties they must attend to as well.
As you ponder yonder city a large goblin warrior moves up to you seemingly unafraid to confront you face to face.  Guard: "Umgh!  What be your business with clan Hollowtooth?"

We here on behalf of the village to the north.  That sow leader of yours had their well poisoned and now we aim to set things right!  Guard: "Dis dat so!  You scrawny pip-squeaks.  Your puny plan is doomed to fail before yer git started.  Attack!"
Another group of warriors forms to attack.  They charge like crazed dogs!
Having seen their comrades fall in battle another group of warriors forms up to avenge them.

You see a large toad of a goblin shouting orders to a group of warriors.  That must be Greshim.  A larger goblin you have never seen.   He is accompanied by three large guards of an unknown race.  He orders an attack but does not attack himself.
Greshim: "You dogs!  Can't you take out a puny handful such as these?  I shall do it myself!"
You spot a large goblin raiding party.  Do you wish to engage them in combat?
With Greshim dead the city erupts in panic.  Wild rumors of how a pack of devils have come to slay all is on everyones lips.  Goblins flee in all directions.
A watch tower.  It is not being used at the time.
A shop.  Most of the goods are shoddy and overpriced.  The selection is also pretty limited.
A temple.  The local shaman are willing to treat you but expect to be paid outlandish prices.

A small lodge filled to overflowing with drunken warriors.  As you try to squeeze past a pair of fat smelly goblins at the door you are rudely shoved back out the door.  "We don't serve your kind in here.  Go make your own mead!"
Guard: "Just you watch yourselves.  We don't get too many wanderers around here and can't say as we care for the few we do get."
This geyser is extremely hot!

As you are peeling the blistering skin from your wounds you notice something near the bottom of a shallow pool in this geyser.  Upon closer inspection you find a dead goblin shaman with her hands bound and a rag stuffed in her mouth.

The meat is literally cooked right off her bones.  She must have fell prey to a would be thief.  However, the thief must have overlooked a small bundle wrapped in a leather wrap.  And what a mistake it was on the thief's part to miss this!
This well has a rank putrid smell.   Poisoned!
The gate to this goblin village swings in a stiff desert breeze.  The stink of dead bodies rotting in the sun hangs heavy in the air.  Not a sole is stirring in this once thriving village.
Desert carrion flies are everywhere.  They are crawling all over the dead bodies and then landing on you.  Save Vs. Vitality or contract a disease.

You find the dead body of  the village chief.  It is the only body you see that looks to have any items you could use.  Just what it is or where it came from is a mystery.  It is nothing like anything you have ever seen before.
Looking at it closely it defies description.  It appears to be magical yet it is not magical in make or nature.  A baffling mystery to be sure.
You see a large pit of vipers!  They appear unwilling to attack as they are guarding a large clutch of eggs.  Do you attack?
You are met by Yancy who greets you with a warm smile.  He sees the huge sack of Ulrick Snake eggs you have with you.  Yancy: "I must admit.  I never figured you would ever come back with those eggs.

So many eggs must have been a great burden for those of your small stature.  I was so sure I would never see you again that I made a bet with Marduke to that affect.  Seems I have lost and Marduke is going to make me live up to my bargain."

Yancy reaches under his robe and pulls out a small wand.  Yancy: "Choose three volunteers for me to enchant.  This wand has but three charges left.  It will make you resistant to chemical attacks for the remainder of your lives."  Choose three.
Never again will I doubt the courage and the bravery of the small folk."  Yancy hands you the items and bids you to stay for a while and rest.
A large area filled with dried foodstuffs.  They appear to be just heaped in the corner without any thought of organization.

A large hall enclosed by great iron bound doors.  At the far side of the room you see a burning coal pit.  Thick black soot covers the ceiling as the concept of a chimney did not enter into the minds of those that built this place.
Strange looking plants are growing the cracks in the floor.  Tender looking berries are sprouting from the bushes.
The bushes are all bare of fruit except this one.  This bush has one single berry that looks to be very plump and juicy.  Do you wish to eat it?
Who will partake of the delectable berry?
You feel different somehow but you can't quite put into words as to how.

You see a large untidy room.  It is guarded by a large force of goblin warriors.  Guard: "You there!  You better get out.  This be the private room of big chief.  You get out or we stick you good!"  Do you leave?
The clamor of battle has caught the attention of the entire fortress.  A large platoon of archers are the first to arrive.
Nothing but a few coins and some old rags.
Some ordinary gear.

You see a human figure clad in red robes and holding a staff.  Man: "Who are you?  Are you the ones responsible for all the turmoil?  I have been working with clan Hollowtooth for years to try and bring them under my control.
I nearly had them charmed to the point of worshipping me as a god.  Now that is all ruined and I dare say you have made me most angry!"

As Marcus Vilewing collapses to the floor in agony he spits a curse upon you.  Marcus Vilewing: "You have not seen the last of me!  I have a power you can't dare conceive of.  We shall meet again.   Very soon I shall think."

You hear a beastly scream behind you.  You spin to see a large dragon closing on your position.  Marcus Vilewing: "Fools!  Now you see my true form.  I shall brush you aside like a child's plaything!"
The body of Marcus Vilewing explodes into thousands of tiny shards of frozen ice!
To enter this area you need to enter your registration code:  At this time enter your registration name?

A few heavy set men are busy at the forge of this large blacksmiths shop.  Sweat and soot run down the brow of a muscular man.  He swears as a spark lands on his cheek.  Blacksmith: "Great Vickers Ghost!  These damn iron hinges will be the death of me."
You quiz the blacksmith on his work.  Blacksmith: "These damnable iron hinges have to be made to replace those stolen from the front gate.  I would give anything to have those Mithril hinges back."
Party: "Just what would you give?" you ask.  Blacksmith: "Plenty!  All I have in fact."  With that curt reply he returns to his work with a sour look on his face.

Blacksmith: "Glory be!  The missing hinges to the front gate.  You found em!  Don't suppose you would be willing to let me have em do ya?"  Party: "What do you offer in return?"  Blacksmith: "All I have really is my thanks.  Be that enough for ya?"
Blacksmith: "I thank ya kindly.  Though I can't offer you any coins for helping me out you do have my thanks."
You come to a lavish mansion.  The servant of the manor asks you to leave as it is the private manor of Lord Melvin.
The servant of this large manor asks you inside.  He speaks to you with great respect.  An elderly gentleman comes to speak with you.  Lord Melvin: "Good day my fine people.

Rory the blacksmith tells me you were kind enough to return the missing gate hinges to him earlier.  I have always had a fondness for Rory.  It pains me so to see him work so hard.   He saved my life a few years back.

I have offered to pay for his retirement but he will have nothing of it.  Please, let me reward  you for making his workaday life a tad bit easier."   Take this.  It is of great value to those in your obvious profession.

Lord Melvin hands a small vial to each of you.  Lord Melvin: "Please, drink it.  I assure you it is quite safe."  Timid at first you each drink the sweet tasting liquid.  Lord Melvin: "I had these made for Rory to aid him in his physically demanding work.

He is distrustful of magic however, and refused to drink them.  They would have made him the most robust blacksmith in all the Realmz.  For you however I would imagine it may aid you in battle."  Each member gains +1 to damage in Hand to Hand combat.
Lord Melvin: "Well, I must return to my daily routine.  I bid you good day."
You loose your footing as the ground beneath you gives way.
A well of cool fresh water is bubbling up from some underground river.

You smell something odd about this well.  It has a taint to it like the scent of rotting flesh.  You drop a torch into the well and watch as it plummets to the water some 100 feet below.  Halfway down you see a creature clawing its way up the side.

You stare in amazement as the nimble creature seems to find hand holds where none exist as it rapidly climbs to the surface.  Right behind it is a whole horde of creatures.  You here a sudden ear splitting screech.

You also hear screeching coming from the other wells as well.  A veritable horde is invading this small village and is using the wells as a way in.  The Troglodytes attack but are no match for the Aqua Men.
You see a wall of stalagmites that block your path.  They soon become too sharp and jagged to cross forcing you to back up.
The only way into the village beyond is through a heavily guarded path straight ahead.  Troglodytes guard it and do not seem willing to let you pass.  Do you wish to parlay?
Troglodyte: "You no get our water.  You no Troglodyte, you no drink."  All your attempts to communicate end the same way.
You are attacked by a band of Troglodyte determined to defend their freshwater wells.
The Troglodytes are nearly wiped out.  However, there seem no end to the Aqua Men pouring out of the wells.   You hear something that sounds more fierce that the Aqua Men as well.

Coming from one of the wells is an Aqua Man of an immense size.  It towers above the other Aqua men.  It lumbers your way, stepping on one of the smaller Aqua men that failed to get out of the way.  The unfortunate Aqua Mans head pops like a ripe grape.

You have slain all of the Aqua Men and the few Troglodytes left alive are badly wounded and will not survive.  You spot a small tunnel that enter the side of one of the wells.  Do you wish to follow it back to where the Aqua Men came from?

As you prepare to ascend you notice a small flow of water near the ground.  You watch it for a few moments as it begins to grow.  The tunnels are beginning to fill with water.  If you leave you will not be able to return.  Do you still want to leave?
You stumble upon a group of Aqua Men working on the tunnel.
You spot a group of Aqua Men.  Do you want to attack them?
You spot a small gap in the wall.  If you exhale you can just squeeze by.

You enter a large sweltering cavern.  To the north you spot many small pools teeming with Aqua Men.  They are thrashing about as these appear to be spawning pools.  They are in such a state of frenzy that they fail to notice you.

You enter a large disgusting egg sack.  It pulses with life.  The inside of the mass is covered with large eggs of newly developing Aqua Men.  You nearly vomit at the very sight.  As you fight to control your stomachs you are surprised by a fat Aqua Man.
It attempts to speak to you but its language is totally unintelligible.  You try to greet it in as many languages as you can muster but they all fail.
Once again it tries to talk to you and still you can't make heads or tails of what it is trying to say.  You are at an impasse.   Neither it nor you seem capable of talking with one another.
You wave your arms around in an effort to try and communicate.  However, the creature is startled by your outlandish movements and runs away.

Slowly you begin to communicate with the fish-like creature.  You soon learn that this is a female and she is not fat but pregnant.  She claims that soon she will deposit her eggs on the walls of this structure where they will grow until they hatch.
Blublub: "We have big problem. Our young no always hatch OK.  Many times they become big and ugly.  We think Troglodyte poison our water.  We kill Troglodyte soon to get poison so we can fix water.

An unoccupied dwelling.  The inhabitant most likely dead from your attack at the front gate.  This hut has walls covered with strange looking animal skins and religious artifacts.  This must have been the hut of the shaman.
You hold out the bottle of Fish Liver Oil but this creature does not seem to know what you want her to do with  it.  She will not go near it.

You explain that you found this strange bottle of Fish Liver Oil in the dwelling of the Troglodyte shaman.  Blublub: "This be poison to our people.  It is easy to fix now we know what is in water.  You are great legend in our stories."

Soon you are surrounded by a whole host of females who wish to thank you for having saved their young.  Blublub: "We wish to honor you with dinner.  Would you like to stay for dinner and be the guests of honor?"

The females become very excited and begin to slowly claw your arms and legs.  It becomes very clear that to be the guest of honor at their dinner means to actually become dinner.  You quickly assemble yourselves and battle your way free.
Sometimes a simple cultural misunderstanding can be  lethal.  You have all suffered many nicks and scratches from sharp claws during your escape and you begin to feel nauseous.

Some form of toxin secreted by the female Aqua Men is invading your body.  The nausea quickly passes but some more long term affects do not.  Each character looses 2 points stamina permanently but gains +1 regeneration per round permanently.
The strangely fat Aqua Man is standing in front of you.  What do you want to do?
You spot a group of strange creatures entering the mouth of the cave.  They appear to be large insects yet they walk upright like a man.  You could hide but would you rather ambush them?
You spot a group of alien creatures headed your way.  Do you wish to ambush them?
You happen upon a thief in the act of murdering two dwarven sentries.  One sentry is already dead and the other is bleeding badly and will surely die without aid.
The poison has finally taken its toll and the dwarf has died.  It must have been a strong poison to kill one so hardy as a dwarf so quickly.

The eyes of the dwarf slowly begin to flutter as the poison is neutralized.  He is soon well enough to stand.  You summon a patrol that is passing by the area to take control of the situation.  Each party member gains 2,500 prestige points.
You managed to save the second dwarf for now but he has been badly poisoned by the blade of the thief.  He will surely die without immediate aid.
You stop the bleeding and heal some of the wounds of this poor sentry.  However, he was poisoned by the blade of the thief and will die without immediate aid.
You stop to converse with the two dwarven sentries.  Sentry: "Have you seen our post to the northwest?  They have not checked in of late and the captain of the guard is not due for another hour."
You pass between two guard towers.  The tower to the southeast has two sentries.  Both are asking if you have seen the captain of the guard.  Perhaps you should speak with them.
You see the body of a dead dwarven sentry.  The brain of this poor dwarf has been sucked out of his skull.   Ick!

This casket has been desecrated only recently.  The body that was once inside has been pulled apart limb from limb.   Nothing remains but a few odd looking coins.  They are not coins, nothing else can describe them better.
Two dead bodies are slumped over the sides of this small boat.  Both have been horribly maimed and the brains sucked from their skulls.  At the stern of the ship is a sack with some strange objects.
The narrow river that feeds this underground lake ends here.  You see some muddy footprints on the shore.

You see several humanoids as well as a number of what can only be described as "Mechanical Creatures" standing guard over a large pen of purple creatures.  One of the humanoids is tossing the severed heads of a few cave lizards into the pen.

You watch in horror as the purple creatures shamble over to the severed heads.  They place the heads near some tentacles on their mouths and literally extract the brains from the skulls.  Do you wish to put an end to this abomination?
One of the Golian warriors programs a probe to open the pens.  It quickly zooms to the animal pen and lowers some sort of power wall and releases only a few of the large purplish creatures within.

A powerful energy field blocks your path.  You can't enter the pen nor can the Alien Vrap escape.  You notice several small disk shaped indentations near what would be the control panel.  They are of various sizes and shapes.
What you thought were coins were actually some sort of bizarre key.  You place the small keys into the indentations and the energy field dissipates.
You are now free to exchange cultural ideas, artistic concepts and family values with the alien Vrap.  However, they seem more interested in just sucking your brains out. (Your typical Alien Vrap!)
On the western edge of the pen you spot a small pile of the alien war machines.  They are unlike those you fought before.
These machines appear to be damaged or broken.  You fiddle around with the alien war machines in an attempt to fix them but nothing seems to work.

You locate a small panel on each machine that is in the same general shape as the power core.  You place a power core inside a machine and it starts up.  It flashes a few lights for a moment or two and announces in a language you can barely understand.
Probe: "Language Subsystems Reset. All Systems Nominal.  Re calibrate Bio Command Module.  Unit ready."
Nothing much of interest.
The guards toss you out on your ear.  Guards: "You have no reason to be looking in the kings chest.  Get out!"
The kings cleric welcomes you to his temple.
The kings cook offers you whatever provisions you wish.  Cook: "You look to be a tad thin.  Take a few morsels."
You find a barrel full of torches as well as some oil flasks.
You see many of the kings warriors resting.  They are busy eating and restocking any provisions they may need for their patrols.

You see the body of Maxwell crumpled on the ground.  His once portly body is now nothing but a skeletal figure.  Draped on his body are his things.  Whatever Maxwell was at one time, it was surely not natural.
You see a stout dwarven blacksmith working at an open air forge.  He is mumbling under his breath as he hammers a large section of steel into a breast plate.

He looks up for a moment and says in a gruff tone.  Dwarf: "Me be hating to use but normal steel in me work but there be no Mithril in town to work with.  You fetch me enough mithril to finish these three suits of armor, and I can let you have one.
Me be willing to sell you a few items as well if you like."
Dwarf: "Ha!  I see you have some Mithril with ya.  I can work that into some pretty nice armor.  If you let me have it, I can let you have one of these suits of armor as payment."  Do you agree?
Dwarf: "Dat be the best of the three.  Wear it well me friends.  Now I have much work to do.  Good day."
You see a hostile looking group ahead.  Do you wish to engage them in combat?
You see a small group of elven adventurers being attacked by a large force of Thrultain.  Do you wish to help the elves in this battle?

A wounded but grateful elven paladin thanks you for your aid.  Paladin: "Many thanks be to you my friends.  The path to prosperity shall be always at your feet.  Though a simple servant am I, shall I forever be in your dept."
Each member who survived the battle gains +1500 prestige.
Flibli falls in battle.  The powerful Elementals he summoned to aid him can't remain without his spell of summoning.

The sounds of battle echo up just ahead.  You spot a lone gnomish warrior, protected by a trio of powerful earth Elementals.  They are under attack by a group of demonic looking creatures.  Do you wish to aid the Gnome?

Flibli: "Many thanks to you my friends.  Without your aid I would surely have perished.  I was but a simple messenger sent to Winterhaven.  I have been tasked to open up talks between my people and the council of Winterhaven.

I have little with which to reward you.  I am sure that my superiors would wish to thank you in person.  If you ever near the city of  Snelflinbig just mention my name to the council and tell your take of heroics. I am sure they would be most grateful.

Here is a crude map that shall show you the secret way to our city.  You must journey a great distance upon the waters of the "Hells Serpent" and it is a dangerous route.  Remember to mention my name if ever you do journey there."  Flibli bids fare well.

You mention the name Flibli and immediately a crowd gathers.  Crowd: "Flibli!  Did you say Flibli!  Is he OK?  Have you seen him?  What do you know of Flibli?"  You relay your take of having aided him in battle against the Psion-Vampires.

Your take of heroics quickly spreads through the village.  Apparently Flibli was a most popular fellow.  An elderly gnome speaks to you.  Anju: "My friends.  Flibli was my most favored of divine pupils.  For many years he did tutor under me.

When I was asked to choose a representative to journey to Winterhaven, he was the obvious choice.  Flibli is as good natured fellow as you will ever meet.  Your having saved his life means the world to me as it does to the whole village.

Please accept this gift not from me, but from her most holy 'Feona of Gnalishbin'.  She has always looked out for those of us who devote our lives to her praise.  Now, let her divine goodness look out for you as well."  Anju hands you a small helm.
Anju: "May the light of Feona bless you always as she does us."
A group of Avians is under attack by a larger force of Harpies, Griffins and Cockatrices.  Would you like to aid the Avians in their fight to stay alive?
The remaining Avians flee to the skies.  A few however are too wounded to fly.  Do you wish to bind their wounds?

You quickly bandage their wounds and cast a few simple spells of healing.  Even so, it will be some time before they can take to the air again.  However, they seem content to remain with you for now.  You gain new allies.

You stop in your tracks as you detect that you are being watched.  In every direction you hear a fait rustling.  Some group of creatures yet unseen is trying to surround you.  Do you form a defensive position or attempt to run away.
Choose Defense
Flee Like Cowards
Within moments you see many sets of glowing blood red eyes appear from the underbrush.
As you clean the sticky ichor from your blades you here another ring of creatures moving in for the kill.
A small school of River Drakes is just off your port quarter.  Do you wish to alter course and intercept them?
You discover an old pirate camp.  It has not been used in many years.  The scurvy dogs even left some of their treasure behind.
You find a small crack in the rubble that has collapsed in the corner.
The crack widens and you see an ornate casket in a dark secluded chamber beyond.
Your bodies are thrown about the room like rag dolls.  Great gouts of flame and raw magical energy pelt you from every direction.

You clasp your heads in agony as hundreds of voices rush into your brain all at once.  As quickly as they started they stop again.  The cacophony is replaced by a sole voice that speaks in a soothing manner.  Voice: "Who dare disturb my rest.

You enter the ruins of an old mansion.  At one time it was an impressive dwelling.  Time and decay however have taken their toll.   As if to illustrate the point, the entire northwest section of the first floor appears to be collapsed.
You find your equipment stashed in the corner.
Who would be so bold as to destroy my pets and invade my house?"

Voice: "I know not of such a thing.  All I do know is that my pets were to guard me so I may rest.  I see now that they were too weak to keep out those such as you.  All I seek is the peace of the afterworld.
I may be able to divine some clues to your search for this "Geyser" of which you speak.  Provided you can do something for me in return.  Do you agree?"
Voice: "Is that so.  Well, I am sure you will be most welcome to it.  Provided you can evict the current resident.  ME!"
Once again your head is flooded with the torturous din of a thousand angry voices.
You see but a simple chair and table.  The table is cluttered with potions.
You see three tombs that radiate magic.
This book is cursed!  The pages fly from the book and land all about you.  Each transforms into a hostile beast!
You marvel at the destructive power of the three cursed books.  You examine them closely and once again they all have their pages as if never read.  Did you wish to read them again?
This time as you page through them you see that they have changed.
Too greedy! Cursed Again!
A table for making oneself presentable.  Most of the powders and oils have long since dried up and become worthless.  There are a few still of value.
A large private chamber.  Everything is in fine order save a thick coating of dust.
A small torture chamber.  The original occupant of the fine bed chamber must have liked to indulge in the more brutal of sins.
This table is covered with instruments of torture.  Most of the devices have long since rusted away.  One however retains the glint of finely honed steel.

A large barracks for the troops that once guarded this fortress.  The skins used for keeping warm have long since decayed to dust.  Piled near each bunk is a set of bones.  It is if the guards were standing at attention and then all instantly died.
You search each of the bodies and the chests near each bed but everything is old and useless.  Full racks near the wall contain old rusted weapons. It's a creepy scene if every you saw one.
An old storeroom.  Currently it stores only decayed sacks of grain and dry bottles of mead.
The cursed spirits of those that once defended this fortress still haunt the halls.
Voice: "Perhaps I could allow you to seek shelter in my humble home.  However, I would ask that you do me a small favor.  Do you agree?"
Voice: "Who am I you ask?  Quite simple my most ignorant friends. I am the one who will drink of your blood like wine from my cup."
Voice: "Well, then.  You must please excuse me.  I have much rest and so little time to chat with the likes of you."  You feel a chilling breeze across your necks as the spirit leaves the area.
Voice: "I gave clear instructions before my untimely death that I was to be buried with my favorite back scratcher.  It's was a simple request but the fools failed to follow my simple instructions.
If you could find my back scratcher, and bring it to me I would be most grateful.  It's located in a secret chamber."  The spirit describes how to locate the chamber as you draw a map.
Voice: "Yippee!  I see you found my back scratcher.  They were such fun to use.  The fond memories this brings back.  Please, hand them over to me."  Do you hand over the Razor Claws?
Voice: "Oh Goody Goody!  Shall I try them out to see if they still work as well as before.  I think I shall.  Here, let me scratch your back!"
A most unique spirit to say the least.  You collect up your Razor Claws once again.
Voice: "Oh bother!  Why do commoners have to be so difficult!  I say, I shall just have to take them."
You give a strong tug on the trap door but see nothing below but a deep pit.
Laying unconscious at the bottom of the pit is a small child.  A large bruise on her head has caused her left eye to swell shut.  You quickly sound the alarm.

A large crowd of concerned dwarves gather around.  A large brute of a dwarf climbs down into the pit with a nimbleness of a small child.  Many thank you as you have surely saved the life of this little girl.

The child is taken to a corner where a priest works on soothing her wounds.  Soon her eyes flutter open.  Suddenly one of the gate guards bursts into the large hall.  Dwarf: "Praetorian Raiders are attacking! Praetorian... ack!"
Halfway through his message a large steel boot crushes him from behind.  A large band of giants storms the main hall.
You defeated the small band of Praetorian Raiders that battled its way into the main hall.   The din of battle rages strong outside in the courtyard.  Do you rush to defend the dwarven city?
Everybody in the hall rushes out to defend their city.  They look at you with obvious disdain at your lack of will to fight.  You loose 5000 prestige.

You emerge into the raging battle in the courtyard.  The dwarven defenses are unorganized.  Leadership is weak.  You spot a trio of high ranking dwarven captains surrounded by a group of Praetorians.  It's vital that they survive.
You have succeeded in pushing the Praetorian Raiders back.  Your dwarven allies begin to rally at the front gate even as the main body of the raiders charge into the dwarven ranks.

You have defeated the best the Praetorian Raiders could muster.  You fall to the ground exhausted when you hear the booming laughter of ogres.  You look up to see a small group of ogres, flanked by even more Praetorian Raiders.  Will it never end?

Exhausted nearly to the point of collapse it would seem you have finally vanquished the hostile invaders.  Few dwarves are left standing to thank you for your aid.  It will take considerable time and money to rebuild this city.
Do you wish to offer to help pay to rebuild this once proud community?
You have fought a hard and bitter battle.  Nobody can blame you as you have helped more than could be expected already.
Such a kind and generous offer goes above and beyond the call of duty.  Each member gains +15000 prestige and gains a level.
